Ascend to the Levanon and cry, and on the Bashan give forth your voice, and cry for Avarim for all your lovers have been broken.
I spoke to you in your peaceful times. You said, "I will not heed." This is your way since your youth, for you did not hearken to My voice.
All your shepherds shall be broken by the wind, and your lovers shall go into captivity, for then you shall be ashamed and confounded because of all your evil.
You, who abide in the Levanon, who nest in the cedars, how gracious shall you be when pangs come to you, the pain of a woman in travail?
As I live, Havayah says, though Konyahu the son of Yehoyakim, king of Yehudah, be a signet on My right hand, from there I will remove you.
And I will deliver you into the hands of those who seek your life and into the hands of those you fear and into the hands of Nevuchadretzar, king of Bavel, and into the hands of the Kasdim.
And I will cast you and your mother who bore you, to another land where you were not born, and there you shall die.
But to the land to which they long to return there, there they shall not return.
Is this man, Konyahu, a despised, shattered image, or a vessel in which there is no use? Why were he and his seed cast away, thrown to a land they know not?
O land, land, land, hearken to the word of Havayah.
So Havayah said: Inscribe this man childless, a man who will not prosper in his days, for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting on the throne of Dovid or ruling anymore in Yehudah.
Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the flocks of My pasture! Havayah says.

Therefore, so Havayah Elokim says of Yisroel concerning the shepherds: You who pasture My people, you have scattered My flocks and have driven them away and have not taken care of them; behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your deeds, Havayah says.
And I will gather the remnant of My flocks from all the lands where I have driven them, and I will restore them to their dwellings and they shall be fruitful and multiply.
And I will set up shepherds over them and they shall pasture them, and they shall no longer fear nor shall they be dismayed, nor shall any of them be missing, Havayah says.
Behold, days are coming, Havayah says, when I will set up of Dovid a righteous shoot, and he shall reign a king and prosper, and he shall perform judgment and righteousness in the land.
In his days, Yehudah shall be saved and Yisroel shall dwell safely, and this is his name that he shall be called, The Havayah is our righteousness.
Therefore, behold days are coming, Havayah says, when they shall no longer say, "As Havayah lives, Who brought up the children of Yisroel from the land of Mitzrayim,"
But, "As Havayah lives, Who brought up and Who brought the seed of the house of Yisroel from the northland and from all the lands where I have driven them, and they shall dwell on their land."
Because of the prophets my heart is broken within me, my bones shake, I was like a drunken man and like a man whom wine has overcome, because of Havayah and because of His holy words.
For the land is full of adulterers, for because of oaths the land mourns, the dwellings in the wilderness are dried out, and their eagerness was evil and their power not right.
For both prophet and priest are false; even in My house have I found their evil, Havayah says.
Therefore, their way shall be for them like slippery places in the dark; let them be thrust and fall therein, for I will bring evil upon them, the year of their visitation, Havayah says.
And in the prophets of Shomron I saw unseemliness; they prophesied by Baal and misled My people Yisroel.

And in the prophets of Yerushalayim I saw a horrible thing, committing adultery and going with falseness, and they encouraged evil-doers, that none returns from his evil; all of them were to Me as Sedom and her inhabitants as Amorah.

Therefore, so Havayah of Hosts said concerning the prophets: Behold I will feed them wormwood and give them poisonous water to drink, for from the prophets of Yerushalayim has falseness emanated to the whole land.
So Havayah of Hosts said: Do not hearken to the words of the prophets who prophesy for you; they mislead you. The vision of their heart they speak, not from the mouth of Havayah.
They say to those who despise Me, "The Havayah has spoken, 'You shall have peace, ' " and to everyone who follows the view of his heart they say, "No evil shall befall you."
For who stood in the council of Havayah and will see and hear His word? He who hearkened to His word and listened.
Behold a storm from Havayah has gone forth with fury, yea, a whirling storm, on the heads of the wicked it shall rest.
The Havayah's anger shall not return until He executes it and until He fulfills the plans of His heart. At the end of days, you shall consider it perfectly.
I did not send the prophets yet they ran; I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied.
And if they stood in My council, they should have let My people hear My words, so that they bring them back from their evil way and from the evil of their deeds.
Am I a Elokim from near, Havayah says, and not a Elokim from afar?
Can a man hide in secret places that I should not see him? Havayah says. Do I not fill the heavens and the earth? Havayah says.
I heard what the prophets said, those who prophesy in My name falsely, saying, "I have dreamed, I have dreamed."
How long will this be? Is it in the heart of the prophets who prophesy lies? But they are prophets of the deceit of their hearts,
Who think to cause My people to forget My name with their dreams that they tell, one to another, as their forefathers forgot My name through Baal.
The prophet who has a dream, let him tell a dream, and who has My word, let him tell My word as truth. What has the straw to do with the wheat? Havayah says.
Is not My word so like fire? Havayah says, and like a hammer that shatters a rock?
Therefore, behold I am against the prophets, Havayah says, those who steal My words from one another.
Behold I am against the prophets, Havayah says, those who train their tongues and say, "He says,"

Behold I am against those who prophesy with false dreams, Havayah says, and they tell them and mislead My people with their falsehoods and with their bewilderment, but I neither sent them nor commanded them, and they have not availed this people, Havayah says.
Now if this people or the prophet or priest asks you, saying, "What is the burden of Havayah?" And you shall say to them, "What burden? And I will forsake you, Havayah says."
And the prophet and the priest and the people who will say, "The burden of Havayah," I will visit retribution upon that man and upon his household.
So shall you say each one to his friend and each one to his brother, "What did Havayah reply?" or "What did Havayah speak?"
And "the burden of Havayah" you shall no longer mention, for the burden shall be to the man of His word although you pervert the words of the living Elokim, Havayah of Hosts, our Elokim.
So shall you say to the prophet, "What has Havayah replied to you?" Or "What has Havayah spoken? "
But if you say, "The burden of Havayah," therefore, so Havayah says, since you have said this thing, "the burden of Havayah," and I sent to you saying, "You shall not say, 'the burden of Havayah,' "
Therefore, here I am, and I will exile you, and I will forsake you and the city that I gave you and your forefathers from before My presence.
And I will place upon you everlasting shame and everlasting embarrassment that shall not be forgotten.

The Havayah showed me two pots of figs, prepared before the Temple of Havayah after Nevuchadretzar, king of Bavel, had exiled Yechonyah son of Yehoyakim king of Yehudah and the princes of Yehudah and the craftsmen and the sentries of the gates from Yerushalayim and brought them to Bavel.
One pot contained very good figs like the first ripe figs, and the other pot contained very bad figs that could not be eaten because they were so bad.
And Havayah said to me; What do you see, Yirmiyahu? And I said, "Figs. The good figs are very good, and the bad ones are very bad, which cannot be eaten because they are so bad."
And the word of Havayah came to me, saying:
So Havayah Elokim said of Yisroel; Like these good figs, so will I recognize the exile of Yehudah, which I have sent forth from this place to the land of the Kasdim, for good.
And I will place My eyes upon them for good, and I will return them to this land, and I will build them and not destroy, and I will plant them and not pluck them.
And I will give them a heart to know Me, for I am Havayah, and they shall be to Me for a people, and I will be to them for a Elokim, for they shall return to Me with all their heart.

And like the bad figs that cannot be eaten because they are so bad, for so Havayah said: So will I make Tzidkiyahu King of Yehudah and his princes and the remnant of Yerushalayim remaining in this land, and those dwelling in the land of Mitzrayim.

And I shall make them for a horror and for evil for all the kingdoms of the earth, for a disgrace and for a proverb, for a conversation piece and for a curse in all the places where I will exile them.
And I will send forth the sword, the famine, and the pestilence against them until they are consumed from upon the land that I gave them and their forefathers.
The word that came to Yirmiyahu concerning all the people of Yehudah in the fourth year of Yehoyakim son of Yoshiyahu, king of Yehudah — that is the first year of Nevuchadretzar king of Bavel.
Which Yirmiyahu the prophet spoke to all the people of Yehudah and to all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, saying:

From the thirteenth year of Yoshiyahu son of Amon, king of Yehudah, until this day, these twenty-three years the word of Havayah has come to me, and I spoke to you, arising early and speaking, but you did not hearken.
And Havayah sent to you all His servants, the prophets, sending them early, but you did not hearken and you did not incline your ears to listen.
Saying; Repent now, each man of his evil way and of the evil of your deeds, and dwell on the land that Havayah gave you and your forefathers from days of yore and forever.
And do not go after other gods to worship them and to prostrate yourselves to them, and you shall not provoke Me with the work of your hands, and I will not harm you.
But you did not hearken to Me, Havayah says, in order to provoke Me with the work of your hands for your harm.
Therefore, so Havayah of Hosts said: Since you have not hearkened to My words,

Behold, I send and I will take all the families of the north, Havayah says, and to Nevuchadretzar the king of Bavel, My servant, and I will bring them upon this land and upon its inhabitants and upon all these nations around, and I will destroy them and make them for a desolation and for a hissing and for perpetual ruins.
And I will cause to cease from them a voice of mirth and a voice of joy, the sound of a bridegroom and the sound of a bride, the sound of a mill and the light of a candle.
And all this land shall become waste and desolation, and these nations shall serve the king of Bavel for seventy years.

And it shall be at the completion of seventy years, I will visit upon the king of Bavel and upon that nation, Havayah says, their iniquity, and upon the land of the Kasdim, and I will make it for everlasting desolations.
And I will bring upon that land all My words that I have spoken about it, all that is written in this book, which Yirmiyahu prophesied concerning all the nations.
For many nations and great kings will enslave them too, and I will recompense them according to their deed and according to the work of their hands.
For so Havayah Elokim said of Yisroel to me; Take this cup of the wine of fury from My hand, and you shall give it to all the nations to whom I send you, to drink.
And they shall drink and reel to and fro and be like madmen because of the sword that I am sending among them.
And I took the cup from the hand of Havayah, and I gave it to all the nations to whom Havayah had sent me, to drink.
Yerushalayim and the cities of Yehudah, and its kings and its princes, to make them a waste, a desolation, a hissing, and a curse, as of this day.
Paroh the king of Mitzrayim and his servants and his princes and all his people.
And all the allies and all the kings of the land of Uz, and all the kings of the land of the Pelishtim and Ashkelon and Azah and Ekron and the remnant of Ashdod.
And Edom and Moav and the children of Ammon.
And all the kings of Tzor and all the kings of Tzidon and the kings of the isle that is on the other side of the area.
Dedan and Teima and Buz and all those separated in that corner.
And all the kings of Arav and all the kings of the allies who dwell in the desert.
And all the kings of Zimri, and all the kings of Eilam and all the kings of Madai.
And all the kings of the north, both near and far, one after the other, and all the kingdoms of the earth that are upon the face of the earth; and the king of Sheishach shall drink after them.
And you shall say to them: So Havayah Elokim said of Yisroel; Drink, become drunk, and vomit, fall and you shall not rise, because of the sword that I am sending among you.
And it shall be, if they refuse to take the cup from your hand to drink, that you shall say to them: So Havayah of Hosts said: You shall surely drink.

For behold, with the city upon which My name is called, I commence to bring evil, and shall you be cleared? You shall not be cleared, for I call a sword upon all the inhabitants of the earth, Havayah of Hosts says.

And you prophesy to them all these words, and you shall say to them: The Havayah shall roar from above, and from His Holy Habitation He shall give forth His voice; He shall roar over His habitation; "Hedad!" He shall call out like those who tread grapes, to all the inhabitants of the earth.
A stirring has come until the end of the earth, for Elokim has a controversy with the nations; He contends with all flesh. The wicked He has delivered to the sword, Havayah says.
So Havayah of Hosts said: Behold evil goes forth from nation to nation, and a great storm shall be awakened from the ends of the earth.

And those slain by Havayah shall be on that day from the end of the earth to the end of the earth; they shall not be lamented; neither gathered nor buried. They shall be as dung on the face of the earth.
Howl, O you shepherds, and cry out, and roll, you mighty of the sheep, for your days have filled to slaughter, and your scatterings, and you shall fall as a precious vessel.
And flight shall fail the shepherds and deliverance the mighty of the flock.
Hark! the cry of the shepherds and the howling of the mighty of the flocks, for Havayah plunders their pasture.
And the tranquil abodes shall be destroyed because of Havayah's furious wrath.
He has left His hut like a young lion, for their land has become waste, because of the wrath of the oppressing sword, and because of His furious wrath.
In the beginning of the reign of Yehoyakim the son of Yoshiyahu, the king of Yehudah, this word came from Havayah, saying:

So Havayah said: Stand in the court of the house of Havayah, and you shall speak to all the cities of Yehudah that come to prostrate themselves in the house of Havayah, all the words that I have commanded you to speak to them; do not omit a word.
Perhaps they will heed and repent, each one of his evil way, and I will repent of the evil that I think to do to them because of the evil of their deeds.
And you shall say to them: So Havayah said, If you do not heed Me to walk in My law that I have placed before you,
To heed the words of My servants, the prophets, whom I send to you betimes, and you did not heed.
I will make this house like Shiloh and this city I will make into a curse to all the nations of the earth.
And the priests and the prophets and all the people heard Yirmiyahu speaking these words in the house of Havayah.

And it came to pass when Yirmiyahu finished speaking all that Havayah had commanded him to speak to all the people, that the priests, the prophets, and all the people seized him, saying, "You shall surely die.

Why have you prophesied in the name of Havayah, saying, 'This house shall be like Shiloh, and this city shall be desolate without an inhabitant'?" And all the people congregated upon Yirmiyahu in the house of Havayah.
And the princes of Yehudah heard these words and went up from the king's house to the house of Havayah, and they sat at the entrance of the new gate of Havayah.
And the priests and the prophets said to the princes and to all the people, saying, "This man is liable to death, for he prophesied concerning this city, as you have heard with your ears. "
And Yirmiyahu said to all the princes and to all the people saying, "The Havayah sent me to prophesy concerning this house and concerning this city all the words that you have heard.
And now, mend your ways and your deeds and heed Havayah your Elokim, and Havayah will renounce the evil that He has spoken concerning you.
As for me, behold I am in your hands; do to me what you deem good and proper.

But you should know that if you put me to death, that you are bringing innocent blood upon yourselves and upon this city and upon its inhabitants, for indeed Elokim sent me concerning you, to speak into your ears all these words."
And the princes and all the people said to the priests and to the prophets, "This man is not liable to the death sentence, for he spoke to us in the name of Havayah our Elokim."
Then certain of the elders of the land rose and said to all the congregation of the people, saying:

Michah the Morashiti was prophesying in the days of Chizkiyahu the king of Yehudah, saying: So Havayah of Hosts said: Tziyon shall be plowed for a field, and Yerushalayim shall be heaps, and the Temple Mount as the high places of a forest.

Did Chizkiyahu and all Yehudah put him to death? Did he not fear Havayah? And he entreated Havayah, and Havayah renounced the evil that He had spoken concerning them. But we are doing great harm to ourselves.
Also a man was prophesying in the name of Havayah, Uriyah the son of Shemayah of Kiryat-Yearim, and he prophesied concerning this city and concerning this land, like all the words of Yirmiyahu.
And King Yehoyakim and all his mighty warriors and all the princes heard his words, and the king sought to put him to death, and Uriyah heard and he was afraid, and he fled and came to Mitzrayim.
And King Yehoyakim sent men to Mitzrayim, Elnatan son of Achbor and men with him to Mitzrayim.
And they took Uriyah out of Mitzrayim and brought him to King Yehoyakim, and he struck him with the sword and cast his corpse into the graves of the common people.
But the hand of Achikam the son of Shafan was with Yirmiyahu, not to deliver him into the hands of the people to put him to death.
In the beginning of the reign of Yehoyakim the son of Yoshiyahu, king of Yehudah, this word came to Yirmiyahu from Havayah, saying:
So Havayah said to me; Make yourself thongs and bars, and place them upon your neck.

And you shall send them to the king of Edom and to the king of Moav and to the king of the children of Ammon and to the king of Tzor and to the king of Tzidon by the hand of ambassadors who come to Yerushalayim to Tzidkiyahu, the king of Yehudah.
And you shall command them to their masters, saying: So Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; so shall you say to your masters:
I made the earth, the man and the beast that are upon the face of the earth, with My great strength and with My outstretched arm, and I gave it to him that pleased Me.
And now, I have given these lands into the hand of Nevuchadnetzar the king of Bavel, My servant, and even the beasts of the field I have given to him to serve him.
And all nations shall serve him and his son and his son's son until the time of his own land come, and many nations and great kings shall make him servile.

And it shall come to pass that the nation or the kingdom that will not serve him, Nevuchadnetzar the king of Bavel, and who will not place his neck into the yoke of the king of Bavel, with the sword and with famine and with pestilence will I visit upon that nation, Havayah says, until I have consumed them by his hand.
And you, heed not your prophets or your diviners or your dreams or your soothsayers or your sorcerers, who say to you, saying, "You shall not serve the king of Bavel."
For they are prophesying falsely to you in order to remove you far from your land, and so that I will drive you out and you will perish.
And as for the nation that will bring his neck into the yoke of the king of Bavel and serve him, I will allow him to remain on his soil, Havayah says, and he will till it and dwell on it.
And to Tzidkiyahu the king of Yehudah have I spoken according to all these words, saying, "Bring your necks into the yoke of the king of Bavel and serve him and his people, and live.
Why should you die, you and your people, by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence, as Havayah has spoken concerning the nation that will not serve the king of Bavel?
And do not heed the words of the prophets who say to you, saying, "You shall not serve the king of Bavel," for they are prophesying falsely to you.
For I have not sent them, Havayah says, and they are prophesying in My name falsely, in order that I drive you out and that you perish, you and the prophets who are prophesying to you.

And to the priests and to all this people I have spoken, saying: So Havayah said: Heed not the words of your prophets who prophesy to you, saying, "Behold, the vessels of the house of Havayah will be returned from Bavel now hastily," for they are prophesying falsely to you.
Heed them not; serve the king of Bavel, and live. Why should this city be destroyed?

But if they are prophets, and if the word of Havayah is with them, let them now entreat Havayah of Hosts that the vessels remaining in the house of Havayah and in the house of the king of Yehudah and in Yerushalayim not come to Bavel.
For so has Havayah of Hosts said concerning the pillars, concerning the sea, and concerning the bases, and concerning the rest of the vessels remaining in this city.
Which Nevuchadnetzar king of Bavel did not take when he exiled Yechonyah son of Yehoyakim, king of Yehudah, from Yerushalayim to Bavel, and all the nobles of Yehudah and Yerushalayim.
For so Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel, concerning the vessels remaining in the house of Havayah and in the house of the King of Yehudah and Yerushalayim:
They shall be brought to Bavel, and there they shall be until the day I remember them, Havayah said, and I will bring them up and restore them to this place.

And it came to pass in that year, in the beginning of the reign of Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah, in the fourth year in the fifth month, Chananyah the son of Azur, the prophet who was from Givon, said to me in the house of Havayah before the eyes of the priests and all the people, saying:
So Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel, saying: I have broken the yoke of the king of Bavel.
In another two years, I will restore to this place all the vessels of the house of Havayah, that Nevuchadnetzar the king of Bavel has taken from this place and brought to Bavel.
And Yechonyah the son of Yehoyakim the king of Yehudah and all the exile of Yehudah coming to Bavel, I will restore to this place, Havayah says, for I will break the yoke of the king of Bavel.
And Yirmiyahu the prophet said to Chananyah the prophet before the eyes of the priests and before the eyes of all the people standing in the house of Havayah.

And Yirmiyahu the prophet said, "Amen! So may Havayah do. May Havayah fulfill your words that you have prophesied, to return the vessels of the house of Havayah and all the exile from Bavel to this place.
But, hearken now to this thing that I speak in your ears and in the ears of all the people.
The prophets who were before me and before you of old, and prophesied concerning many lands and great kingdoms for war and for evil and for pestilence
The prophet who would prophesy for peace, when the word of the prophet would come, the prophet whom Havayah had truly sent would be known.
And Chananyah the prophet took the bar off the neck of Yirmiyahu the prophet and broke it.

And Chananyah said before the eyes of all the people, saying: So Havayah said: So will I break the yoke of Nevuchadnetzar king of Bavel, in another two full years, off the neck of all the nations. And Yirmiyahu the prophet went on his way.
And the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu after Chananyah the prophet had broken the bar off the neck of Yirmiyahu the prophet, saying:
Go and say to Chananyah, saying: So Havayah said: Bars of wood have you broken, and you shall make in their stead bars of iron.

For so Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; An iron yoke have I placed upon the neck of all these nations to serve Nevuchadnetzar king of Bavel, and they shall serve him, and also the beasts of the field have I given to him.
And Yirmiyahu the prophet said to Chananyah the prophet: The Havayah did not send you, and you assured this people with a lie.
Therefore, so Havayah said: Behold I send you off the face of the earth; this year you shall die, for you have spoken perversion against Havayah.
And Chananyah the prophet died in that year, in the seventh month.

And these are the words of the scroll that Yirmiyahu the prophet sent from Yerushalayim to the remaining elders of the exile and to the priests and to the prophets and to all the people that Nevuchadnetzar had exiled from Yerushalayim to Bavel.
After Yechonyah the king and the queen-mother and the officers, the princes of Yehudah and Yerushalayim, and the craftsmen and the gate sentries had left Yerushalayim.
In the hand of Elasah the son of Shafan and Gemaryahu the son of Chilkiyah, whom Tzidkiyahu the king of Yehudah had sent to Nevuchadnetzar the king of Bavel to Bavel, saying:
So Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel, to all the exile which I have exiled from Yerushalayim to Bavel:
Build houses and dwell therein, and plant gardens and eat their produce.
Take wives and beget sons and daughters, and take wives for your sons and give your daughters to men, and they shall bear sons and daughters, and multiply there and be not diminished.
And seek the peace of the city where I have exiled you and pray for it to Havayah, for in its peace you shall have peace.
For so Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; Let not your prophets who are in your midst or your diviners mislead you, neither shall you heed your dreams, which you cause to dream.
For they prophesy to you falsely in My name; I have not sent them, Havayah says.
For so Havayah said: For at the completion of seventy years of Bavel I will remember you, and I will fulfill My good word toward you, to restore you to this place.
For I know the thoughts that I think about you, Havayah says, thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you a future and a hope.
And you shall call Me and go and pray to Me, and I will hearken to you.
And you will seek Me and find Me for you will seek Me with all your heart.

And I will be found by you, Havayah says, and I will return your captivity and gather you from all the nations and from all the places where I have driven you, Havayah says, and I will return you to the place whence I exiled you.
For you have said: The Havayah has set up prophets for us in Bavel.
For so Havayah said concerning the king who sits on the throne of Dovid and concerning the entire people that dwells in this city: Your brethren who have not left with you into exile.
So Havayah of Hosts said: Behold I incite upon them the sword, the famine, and the pestilence, and I will make them as the loathsome figs, which cannot be eaten because they are so bad.

And I will pursue them with the sword, with the famine, and with the pestilence, and I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, for an oath, for astonishment, for hissing, and for a reproach among all the nations where I have exiled them.
Because they have not hearkened to My words, Havayah says, which I sent to them with My servants, the prophets, sending them betimes, but you did not hearken, Havayah says.
Now you, hearken to the word of Havayah, all the exile that I have sent away from Yerushalayim to Bavel.

So Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel, concerning Achav the son of Kolayah and concerning Tzidkiyahu the son of Maaseiyah, who prophesy to you falsely in My name: Behold I deliver them into the hands of Nevuchadnetzar the king of Bavel, and he shall slay them before your eyes.
And a curse shall be taken from them by the entire exile of Yehudah which is in Bavel, saying: May Havayah make you like Tzidkiyahu and like Achav, whom the king of Bavel burnt with fire.

Because they committed a disgrace in Yisroel, and they committed adultery with the wives of their neighbors, and they spoke false things in My name, which I had not commanded them, and I am He Who knows and a witness, Havayah says.
And to Shemayah the Nechelami, you shall say, saying:

So Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel, saying: Because you sent in your name letters to the entire people that is in Yerushalayim and to Tzefanyah the son of Maaseiyah the priest and to all the priests, saying:

The Havayah made you a priest instead of Yehoyada the priest, to be officers in the house of Havayah, over every man who is mad and makes himself a prophet, that you should put him into the prison or into the stocks.
And now, why have you not rebuked Yirmiyahu the Anatoti, who is prophesying to you?
Forasmuch as he sent to us to Bavel, saying: It is long; build houses and dwell, and plant gardens and eat their produce.
And Tzefanyah the priest read this letter in the ears of Yirmiyahu the prophet.
And the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu, saying:
Send to all the exile, saying: So Havayah said concerning Shemayah the Nechelami: Since Shemayah prophesied to you although I did not send him, and he assured you with a lie.

Therefore, so Havayah said: Behold I will visit on Shemayah the Nechelami and upon his seed that he shall have no man sitting in the midst of this people, and he shall not see the good that I am doing to My people, Havayah says, for he spoke perversion against Havayah.
The word that came to Yirmiyahu from Havayah, saying:
So Havayah said, the Elokim of Yisroel, saying: Write for you the words that I have spoken to you, on a scroll.

For, behold, days are coming, Havayah says, when I will restore the captivity of My people Yisroel and Yehudah, Havayah says, and I will restore them to the land that I gave their forefathers and they shall possess it.
And these are the words that Havayah spoke concerning Yisroel and concerning Yehudah.
For so Havayah said: A sound of quaking we have heard, fear, and there is no peace.
Ask now and see whether a male gives birth. Why have I seen every man with his hands on his loins like a woman in confinement, and every face has turned to pallor?
Ho! For that day is great, with none like it, and it is a time of distress for Yackov, through which he shall be saved.
And it shall be on that day, Havayah of Hosts says, that I will break his yoke off your neck, and I will break your thongs, and strangers shall no longer enslave them.
And they shall serve Havayah their Elokim and Dovid their king, whom I will set up for them.

And you, fear not, My servant Yackov, Havayah says, and do not be dismayed, O Yisroel, for behold I save you from afar and your seed from the land of their captivity, and Yackov shall again be silent and at ease, and no one will frighten them.

For I am with you, Havayah says, to save you, for I will make an end of all the nations where I dispersed you, but of you I will not make an end, but I will chasten you in measure, and I will not completely destroy you.
For so Havayah said: Your injury is painful, your wound grievous.
No one deems your wound to be healed, you have no healing medicines.
All your lovers have forgotten you, they do not seek you, for I have smitten you with the wound of an enemy, cruel chastisement, for the greatness of your iniquity; your sins are many.
Why do you cry about your injury that your pain is severe? For the magnitude of your iniquity, since your sins are many, I have done these to you.

Therefore, all who devour you shall be devoured, and all your adversaries, yea all of them, shall go into captivity, and those who plunder you shall be plunder, and all who prey upon you I will give for prey.
For I will bring healing to you, and of your wounds I will heal you, Havayah says, for they called you an outcast, that is Tziyon whom no one seeks out.

So Havayah said: Behold I am returning the captivity of the tents of Yackov, and his dwellings I will pity, and the city shall be built on its mound and the palace on its proper site shall be established.

And thanksgiving and the voice of those making merry shall proceed from them, and I will multiply them, and they shall not be diminished, and I will increase them, and they shall not become few in number.
And their children shall be as of old, and their congregation shall be established before Me, and I will visit evil upon all their oppressors.

And their prince shall be from them, and their ruler shall emerge from their midst, and I will bring him near, and he shall approach Me, for who is it who pledged his heart to approach Me? Havayah says.
And you shall be My people, and I will be your Elokim.
Behold a storm from Havayah has gone forth with fury, yea a settling storm; on the heads of the wicked it shall rest.
The kindling of Havayah's anger shall not return until He has executed it, and until He has fulfilled the plans of His heart. At the end of the days you shall consider it.
At that time, Havayah says, I will be the Elokim of all the families of Yisroel, and they shall be My people.
So Havayah says: In the wilderness, the people who had escaped the sword found favor; He therefore went to give Yisroel their resting place.
From long ago, Havayah appeared to me; With everlasting love have I loved you; therefore have I drawn you to Me with loving-kindness.
Yet again will I rebuild you, then you shall be built, O virgin of Yisroel; yet again shall you be adorned with your tambourines, and you shall go out with the dances of those who make merry.
Yet again shall you plant vineyards on the mountains of Shomron, indeed planters shall plant them and redeem them.
For there is a day, the watchers shall call on the mountains of Efraim; Rise! Let us go up to Tziyon, to Havayah, our Elokim.
For so Havayah says to Yackov, "Sing with joy and shout at the head of the nations, make it heard, praise, and say, 'O Havayah, help Your people, the remnant of Yisroel!' "

Behold I bring them from the north country and gather them from the uttermost ends of the earth, the blind and the lame amongst them, the woman with child and she who travails with child all together; a great company shall they return there.

With weeping will they come, and with supplications will I lead them, along brooks of water will I make them go, on a straight road upon which they will not stumble, for I have become a Father to Yisroel, and Efraim is My firstborn.
Hear the word of Havayah, O nations, and declare it on the islands from afar, and say, "He Who scattered Yisroel will gather them together and watch them as a shepherd his flock.
For Havayah has redeemed Yackov and has saved him out of the hand of him who is stronger than he.

And they shall come and jubilate on the height of Tziyon, and they will stream to the goodness of Havayah, over corn, wine, and oil, and over sheep and cattle, and their soul shall be like a well-watered garden, and they shall have no further worry at all.

Then shall the virgin rejoice in the round dance with music, and the young men and the old men together, and I will turn their mourning into joy and will comfort them and make them rejoice from their sorrow.
And I will refresh the soul of the priests with fat, and My people — they will be satisfied with My goodness, is the word of Havayah.
So Havayah says: A voice is heard on high, lamentation, bitter weeping, Rachel weeping for her children, she refuses to be comforted for her children for they are not.
So Havayah says: Refrain your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for there is reward for your work, Havayah says, and they shall come back from the land of the enemy.
And there is hope for your future, Havayah says, and the children shall return to their own border.
I have indeed heard Efraim complaining, saying, "You have chastised me, and I was chastised as an ungoaded calf, O lead me back, and I will return, for You are Havayah, my Elokim.
For after my return I have completely changed my mind, and after I had been brought to know myself, I smote upon my thigh; I was ashamed, yea I stood confounded, for I bore the reproach of my youth."

"Is Efraim a son who is dear to Me? Is he a child who is dandled? For whenever I speak of him, I still remember him: therefore, My very innards are agitated for him; I will surely have compassion on him," Havayah says.
Set up markers for yourself, place small palms for yourself, put your heart to the highway, the road upon which you went. Return, O virgin of Yisroel, return to these your cities.
How long will you hide, O backsliding daughter? For Havayah has created something new on the earth, a woman shall go after a man.

So Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; They shall yet say this thing in the land of Yehudah and in its cities when I return their captivity; May Havayah bless You, dwelling of righteousness, holy mount.
And Yehudah shall dwell therein and in all its cities together, farmers and those who travel with flocks.
For I have sated the faint soul, and every worried soul have I replenished.
Thereupon, I awoke and I had seen, and my sleep was pleasant to me.
Behold days are coming, Havayah says, and I will sow the house of Yisroel and the house of Yehudah with seed of man and seed of beasts.
And it shall be, as I have watched over them to uproot and to break down, to demolish and to destroy and to afflict, so will I watch over them to build and to plant, Havayah says.
In those days, they shall no longer say, "Fathers have eaten unripe grapes, and the teeth of the children shall be set on edge."
But each man shall die for his iniquity; whoever eats the unripe grapes — his teeth shall be set on edge.
Behold, days are coming, Havayah says, and I will form a covenant with the house of Yisroel and with the house of Yehudah, a new covenant.

Not like the covenant that I formed with their forefathers on the day I took them by the hand to take them out of the land of Mitzrayim, that they broke My covenant, although I was a master over them, Havayah says.

For this is the covenant that I will form with the house of Yisroel after those days, Havayah says: I will place My law in their midst and I will inscribe it upon their hearts, and I will be their Elokim and they shall be My people.

And no longer shall one teach his neighbor or shall one teach his brother, saying, "Know Havayah," for they shall all know Me from their smallest to their greatest, Havayah says, for I will forgive their iniquity and their sin I will no longer remember.
So Havayah said, Who gives the sun to illuminate by day, the laws of the moon and the stars to illuminate at night, Who stirs up the sea and its waves roar, Havayah of Hosts is His name.
If these laws depart from before Me, Havayah says, so will the seed of Yisroel cease being a nation before Me for all time.
So Havayah said: If the heavens above will be measured and the foundations of the earth below will be fathomed, I too will reject all the seed of Yisroel because of all they did, Havayah says.
Behold days are coming, Havayah says, and the city shall be built to Havayah, from the tower of Chananel until the gate of the corner.
And the measuring line shall go out further opposite it upon the hill of Gareb, and it shall turn to Goah.

And the whole valley of the dead bodies and the ash and all the fields until the Kidron Valley, until the corner of the Horse Gate to the east, shall be holy to Havayah; it shall never again be uprooted or torn down forever.
The word that came to Yirmiyahu from Havayah in the tenth year of Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah; that is the eighteenth year of Nevuchadnetzar.
Then, the army of the king of Bavel was besieging Yerushalayim, and Yirmiyahu the prophet was imprisoned in the prison yard that was in the house of the king of Yehudah.
For Tzidkiyahu the king of Yehudah had imprisoned him, saying, "Why do you prophesy, saying, 'So Havayah said: Behold I deliver this city into the hands of the king of Bavel, and he shall capture it.

And Tzidkiyahu the king of Yehudah shall not escape from the hands of the Kasdim, for he shall surely be delivered into the hands of the king of Bavel, and his mouth shall speak with his mouth, and his eyes shall see his eyes.
And he shall lead Tzidkiyahu to Bavel, and he shall be there until I remember him, Havayah says; if you wage war with the Kasdim, you shall not succeed'?"
And Yirmiyahu said: The word of Havayah came to me, saying:
Behold, Chanamel, the son of Shallum your uncle, is coming to you, saying: Buy for yourself my field that is in Anatot, for the right of redemption is yours to buy it.

Then Chanamel, my uncle's son, came to me in the prison yard, according to the word of Havayah, and said to me; Please buy my field that is in Anatot, that is in the country of Binyamin, for the right of inheritance is yours, and you have the right of redemption; buy it for yourself." And I knew that this was the word of Havayah.
So I bought the field from Chanamel, my uncle's son, which was in Anatot, and weighed him the money, seven shekels and ten pieces of silver.
And I wrote a bill of sale and signed it and took witnesses, and weighed the silver on a scale.
And I took the deed of the purchase, that which was signed according to the law and the conditions, and that which was open.

And I gave the deed of the purchase to Baruch the son of Neiriyah the son of Maaseiyah in the presence of Chanamel my uncle and in the presence of the witnesses who signed the deed of purchase, in the presence of all the Yehudim who sat in the prison yard.
And I charged Baruch in their presence, saying:
So Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; Take these scrolls, this deed of purchase and the signed one and this open scroll, and put them into an earthen vessel so that they remain many years.
For so Havayah of Hosts says, the Elokim of Yisroel; Houses and fields and vineyards shall be purchased again in this land.
And I prayed to Havayah after I had delivered the deed of purchase into the hand of Baruch the son of Neiriyah, saying,
"Ho! O Havayah Elokim, behold, You have made the heaven and the earth by Your great power and Your outstretched arm, and nothing is hidden from You,
Who exercises loving-kindness to thousands and requites the iniquity of the fathers in the bosom of the children who follow them, O Great and Mighty Elokim, Havayah of Hosts is His Name.
Who is great in counsel and mighty in carrying it out, for Your eyes are open to all the ways of mankind, to give everyone in accordance with his ways and in accordance with the fruit of his deeds,
Who performed signs and wonders in the land of Mitzrayim until this day, and in Yisroel and in mankind, and have made a name for Yourself as of this day.
And You brought Your people Yisroel forth out of the land of Mitzrayim with signs and with wonders and with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm and with great fearfulness.
And You gave them this land which You swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.

And they came in and took it into possession, but they did not obey You, nor did they walk in Your teachings, all that You commanded them to do they did not do; then You caused all this evil to come upon them.

Behold, the mounds, they have come to the city to take it; by the sword and the famine and the pestilence the city is already given into the hands of the Kasdim who are fighting against it, and what You have proclaimed has come to pass, and lo! You see it.
And You said to me, O Havayah Elokim, 'Buy yourself the field for money and appoint witnesses!' Yet the city is given into the hands of the Kasdim!"
Then the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu, saying:
Behold, I am Havayah, the Elokim of all flesh. Is anything concealed from Me?
Therefore, so Havayah said: Behold I deliver this city into the hands of the Kasdim and into the hands of Nevuchadnetzar the king of Bavel, and he shall capture it.

And the Kasdim who are warring against this city shall come and ignite this city with fire and burn it, and the houses on whose roofs they burnt incense to Baal and offered up libations to strange gods in order to provoke Me.

For the children of Yisroel and the children of Yehudah were indeed doing what is evil in My eyes from their youth, for the children of Yisroel indeed provoke Me with the work of their hands, Havayah says.
For this city has aroused My anger and My wrath since the day they built it until this day, to remove it from before My face.

Because of all the evil of the children of Yisroel and the children of Yehudah, that they did to provoke Me, they, their kings, their officers, their priests, and their prophets, and the people of Yehudah, and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim.
And they turned their backs to Me and not their faces; although I taught them, teaching them betimes, they do not hearken to receive instruction.
And they placed their abominations in the house upon which My Name was called, to contaminate it.

And they built the high places of Baal, which was in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to pass their sons and their daughters to Molech, which I neither commanded them nor did it enter My mind to commit this abomination, in order to bring guilt upon Yehudah.
And now, therefore, so Havayah Elokim said of Yisroel concerning this city which you say, "It has been given into the hands of the king of Bavel by the sword and by famine and by pestilence";
Behold I will gather them from all the lands where I have driven them with My anger and with My wrath and with great fury, and I will restore them to this place and I will cause them to dwell safely.
And they shall be My people, and I will be their Elokim.
And I will give them one accord and one way to fear Me all the time, so that it be good for them and for their children after them.
And I will form for them an everlasting covenant, that I will not turn away from them to do them good, and My fear I will place in their heart, not to turn away from Me.
And I will rejoice over them to do good to them, and I will plant them in this land truly with all My heart and with all My soul.
For so Havayah said: As I have brought upon this people all this great evil, so will I bring upon them all the good that I speak concerning them.
And the field shall be bought in this land, which you say, "It is desolate without man or beast; it has been given into the hands of the Kasdim."

Men shall buy fields for money and inscribe deeds and sign them and appoint witnesses in the land of Binyamin and in the environs of Yerushalayim, and in the cities of Yehudah and in the cities of the mountain and in the cities of the lowland and in the cities of the southland, for I will restore their captivity, Havayah says.
And the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu a second time, while he was still confined in the prison yard, saying:
So Havayah said, the Maker thereof, Who formed it to prepare it; Havayah is His Name.
Call out to Me and I will answer you, and I will tell you great and strong things that you do not know.
For so Havayah Elokim said of Yisroel concerning the houses of this city and concerning the houses of the kings of Yehudah that are demolished for the mounds and for the sword.

They come to war with the Kasdim and to fill them with the corpses of the men whom I have smitten with My anger and with My wrath, and that which I have hidden My face from this city because of all their evil.
Behold, I will bring it healing and cure, and I will cure them, and I will reveal to them a greeting of peace and truth.
And I will return the captivity of Yehudah and the captivity of Yisroel, and build them up like at first.
And I will purify them of all their iniquity that they sinned against Me, and I will forgive all their iniquities that they sinned against Me and that they rebelled against Me.

And it shall be to Me for a name of joy, for praise and for glory to all the nations of the earth who will hear all the good that I do for them and fear and tremble because of all the good and because of all the peace that I do for it.

So Havayah said: There shall again be heard in this place, concerning which you say, "It is desolate without man and without beast," in the cities of Yehudah and in the streets of Yerushalayim that are desolate without a man and without an inhabitant and without a beast,

the sound of mirth and the sound of joy, the voice of a bridegroom and the voice of a bride, the sound of those saying, "Thank Havayah of Hosts, for Havayah is good, for His loving-kindness endures forever," bringing a thanksgiving offering to the House of Havayah, for I will restore the captivity of the land as at first, Havayah said.
So Havayah of Hosts said: There shall again be in this place that is waste without man or beast, and in all its cities a dwelling of shepherds resting their flocks.

In the cities of the mountain, in the cities of the lowland, and in the cities of the Negev and in the land of Binyamin and in the environs of Yerushalayim and in the cities of Yehudah, flocks shall again pass under the hands of one who counts them, Havayah said.
Behold, days are coming, Havayah says, and I will establish the good thing that I spoke concerning the house of Yisroel and the house of Yehudah.
In those days and in that time I will cause to grow for Dovid a plant of righteousness, and he shall execute justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days, Yehudah shall be saved, and Yerushalayim shall dwell securely and this is the name that He shall call it, Havayah is our righteousness.
For so Havayah said: There shall not be cut off from Dovid a man sitting on the throne of the house of Yisroel.
And of the Levi priests, there shall not be cut off from before Me a man offering up a burnt offering, or burning a meal-offering or performing a sacrifice for all time.
And the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu, saying:
So Havayah said: If you break My covenant with the day and My covenant with the night, and not to have day and night in their time.
Also My covenant with Dovid shall be broken, that he should not have a son reigning on his throne, and with the Levi priests, My ministers.
Just as the host of heaven cannot be counted nor can the sand of the sea be measured, so will I increase the seed of My servant Dovid and the Leviim who minister to Me.
And the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu, saying:
Have you not seen what this people has spoken saying: The two families that Elokim chose, He has rejected, and they make My people despise being a nation any longer before them.
So Havayah said: If not My covenant with the day and the night, that the statutes of heaven and earth I did not place,

Also will I reject the seed of Yackov and Dovid, My servant, not to take from his seed rulers over the seed of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yackov, when I bring back their captivity and have mercy upon them.

The word that came to Yirmiyahu from Havayah — when Nevuchadretzar king of Bavel and all his army and all the kingdoms of the land of his rule and all the peoples were waging war against Yerushalayim and against all its cities — saying:

So Havayah Elokim said of Yisroel, Go and say to Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah, and you shall say to him: So Havayah said: Behold I deliver this city into the hands of the king of Bavel, and he shall burn it with fire.

And you shall not escape from his hands, for you shall surely be seized, and you shall be delivered into his hands, and your eyes shall see the eyes of the king of Bavel, and his mouth shall speak with your mouth, and you shall come to Bavel.
But hearken to the word of Havayah, O Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah. So Havayah said concerning you; You shall not die by the sword.

You shall die in peace, and with the burnings of your forefathers, the first kings, who were before you, they shall burn for you, and "Ah master" shall they lament you, for I have spoken a word, Havayah says.
And Yirmiyahu the prophet spoke to Tzidkiyahu king of Yehudah all these words in Yerushalayim.

And the army of the king of Bavel was waging war against Yerushalayim and against all the remaining cities of Yehudah, against Lachish and against Azeikah, because they were the fortified cities left among the cities of Yehudah.
The word that came to Yirmiyahu from Havayah after King Tzidkiyahu had made a covenant with all the people who were in Yerushalayim, to proclaim freedom to them;
That every man should let his manservant and every man his maidservant, a Yehudi and a Yehudis go free, that none should hold his Yehudi brother as a slave.

Now all the princes and all the people who had entered into the covenant hearkened that every one should let his manservant and everyone his maidservant go free, no longer holding them in slavery; then they obeyed and let them go.
But afterwards they turned and brought back the manservants and the maidservants whom they had let free, and forcibly made them into manservants and maidservants.
Then the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu from Havayah, saying:
So Havayah Elokim says of Yisroel; I made a covenant with your fathers on the day that I brought them forth out of the land of Mitzrayim, out of the house of slaves, saying:

"At the end of seven years you shall let go every man his brother Yehudi who has been sold to you, and when he has served you for six years you shall let him go free from you"; but your forefathers did not obey Me, nor did they incline their ears.
And now this day you turned and did what was right in My sight by proclaiming liberty every man to his neighbor, and you made a covenant before Me in the House upon which My Name is called.

But then you turned and profaned My Name, and you took back, each man his manservant and each man his maidservant, whom you had let free to themselves, and forced them to be manservants and maidservants to you.

Therefore, so Havayah says: You have not hearkened to Me to proclaim freedom, every one to his brother and every one to his neighbor; behold I proclaim freedom to you, Havayah says, to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine, and I will make you an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
And I will deliver the men who have transgressed My covenant, who have not kept the words of the covenant which they made before Me when they cut the calf in two and passed between its parts.
The princes of Yehudah and the princes of Yerushalayim, the officers and the priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the parts of the calf.

I will deliver them into the hands of their enemies and into the hands of those who seek their lives, and their dead bodies shall become food for the birds of the heavens and for the beasts of the earth.

And Tzidkiyahu, king of Yehudah, and his princes I will deliver into the hands of their enemies and into the hands of those who seek their lives, and into the hands of the army of the king of Bavel who have gone up away from you.

Behold I command, Havayah says, and I will return them to this city, and they shall fight against it and capture it, and burn it with fire, and the cities of Yehudah I will make desolate without an inhabitant.
The word that came to Yirmiyahu from Havayah in the days of Yehoyakim son of Yoshiyahu, king of Yehudah, saying:
Go to the house of the Reichavim and speak with them, and I will bring them to the House of Havayah, to one of the chambers, and give them wine to drink.
And I took Yaazanyah the son of Yirmiyahu, the son of Chavatzinyah, and his brothers and all his sons and the entire house of the Reichavim.

And I brought them to the House of Havayah, to the chamber of the sons of Chanan the son of Yigdalyahu, the man of Elokim, which is by the chamber of the princes, which is above the chamber of Maaseiyah the son of Shallum, the keeper of the vessels.
And I placed before the sons of the house of the Reichavim goblets full of wine, and cups, and I said to them, "Drink wine."
And they said, "We will not drink wine, for Jonadab the son of Reichav, our father, commanded us saying, "You shall not drink wine, you or your children forever.

And you shall not build a house, neither shall you sow nor shall you plant a vineyard, nor shall you have any, but you shall dwell in tents all your days in order that you live many days on the face of the land where you dwell.
And we hearkened to the voice of Jonadab the son of Reichav, our father, to all that he commanded us, not to drink wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons, and our daughters.
And not to build houses for our dwelling, and not to have a vineyard, a field, or seed.
And we have dwelt in tents, and we have hearkened and done according to all that Jonadab our father has commanded us.

And it came to pass when Nevuchadretzar the king of Bavel came up to the land, that we said, "Come and let us go to Yerushalayim because of the army of the Kasdim and because of the army of Aram, and we dwelt in Yerushalayim."
And the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu, saying:
So Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; Go and say to the men of Yehudah and to the inhabitants of Yerushalayim: Will you not receive instruction to hearken to My words? Havayah says.

The words of Jonadab the son of Reichav, which he commanded his sons not to drink wine, are performed, and they have not drunk wine until this day for they hearkened to the commandment of their father, and I have spoken to you, speaking betimes, yet you have not hearkened to Me.

And I have sent to you all My servants the prophets, sending betimes, saying: Repent now, each man from his evil way and improve your deeds, and do not follow strange gods to worship them, and dwell on the soil that I have given you and your forefathers, but you did not incline your ears, and you did not hearken to Me.
For the sons of Jonadab the son of Reichav have performed the commandment of their father, that he commanded them, but this people has not hearkened to Me.

Therefore, so Havayah Elokim of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; Behold I am bringing upon Yehudah and upon all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim all the evil that I have spoken concerning them, because I spoke to them but they did not obey, and I called out to them, but they did not respond.

And to the house of the Reichavim, Yirmiyahu said: So Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; Because you have obeyed the commandment of Jonadab your father, and you have kept all his commandments and have done according to all that he commanded you,
Therefore, so Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; There shall not be cut off from Jonadab the son of Reichav a man standing before Me for all times.
And it came to pass in the fourth year of Yehoyakim the son of Yoshiyahu the king of Yehudah, that this word came to Yirmiyahu from Havayah, saying:

Take for yourself a roll of a book and write upon it all the words that I have spoken to you concerning Yisroel, concerning Yehudah, and concerning all the nations, since the day that I spoke to you from the days of Yoshiyahu until this day.
Perhaps the house of Yehudah will hear all the evil that I plan to do to them, in order that they should repent, each man of his evil way, and I will forgive their iniquity and their sin.
And Yirmiyahu called Baruch the son of Neiriyah, and Baruch wrote from Yirmiyahu's mouth all the words of Havayah that He had spoken to him, on a roll of a book.
And Yirmiyahu commanded Baruch, saying: I am imprisoned; I cannot enter the House of Havayah.

And you shall come and read in the roll that you have written from my mouth, the words of Havayah, in the ears of the people in the House of Havayah on a fastday, and also in the ears of all of Yehudah who come from their cities, you shall read them.
Perhaps their supplication shall fall before Havayah, and they shall repent, each man of his evil way, for great is the anger and the wrath that Havayah spoke concerning this people.
And Baruch the son of Neiriyah did according to all that Yirmiyahu the prophet had commanded him, to read in the book the words of Havayah in the House of Havayah.

And it came to pass in the fifth year of Yehoyakim the son of Yoshiyahu the king of Yehudah in the ninth month, that they proclaimed a fast before Havayah, all the people in Yerushalayim and all the people coming from the cities of Yehudah who were in Yerushalayim.

And Baruch read in the book the words of Yirmiyahu in the House of Havayah, in the chamber of Gemaryahu the son of Shafan the scribe, in the upper court, at the entrance of the new gate of the House of Havayah, in the ears of all the people.
And Michayahu the son of Gemaryahu the son of Shafan heard all the words of Havayah from upon the book.

And he went down to the house of the king to the chamber of the scribe, and behold there all the officers were sitting; Elishama the scribe and Delayahu the son of Shemayah and Elnatan the son of Achbor and Gemaryahu the son of Shafan and Tzidkiyahu the son of Chananyah and all the officers.
And Michayahu told them all the words that he had heard when Baruch read the book in the ears of the people.

And all the officers sent Yehudi the son of Netanyahu the son of Shelemyahu the son of Kushi to Baruch, saying, "The roll that you read in the ears of the people — take it in your hand and go," and Baruch the son of Neiriyah took the roll in his hand and came to them.
And they said to him, "Sit down now and read it in our ears," and Baruch read in their ears.
And it came to pass when they heard all the words, they feared each man his friend, and they said to Baruch, "We will surely tell the king these words."
And they asked Baruch, saying, "Tell us now how you wrote all these words from his mouth."
And Baruch said to them, "From his mouth he would pronounce all these words to me, and I would write in the book with ink."
And the officers said to Baruch, "Go hide, you and Yirmiyahu, and let no man know where you are."
And they came to the king, to the court, and the roll they deposited in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and they told in the king's ears all the words.
And the king sent Yehudi to take the roll, and he took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and Yehudi read it in the king's ears and in the ears of all the officers standing over the king.
Now the king was sitting in the winter-house in the ninth month, and the brazier was burning before him.

And it came to pass, when Yehudi read three or four verses, he rent it with a scribe's razor, and cast it onto the fire which was on the brazier until the entire roll was consumed on the fire that was on the brazier.
And the king and all his servants who heard all these words were neither frightened nor did they rend their garments.
And also Elnatan and Delayahu and Gemaryahu had entreated the king not to burn the roll, but he heeded them not.
And the king commanded Yerachmeel the king's son and Serayah the son of Azriel and Shelemyahu the son of Avdiel to take Baruch the scribe and Yirmiyahu the prophet, but Havayah concealed them.
And the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu after the king had burnt the roll and the words that Baruch had written from Yirmiyahu's mouth, saying:
Take for yourself again another roll and write upon it all the original words that were on the first roll, which Yehoyakim the king of Yehudah, burned.

And concerning Yehoyakim the king of Yehudah you shall say, So Havayah said: You have burnt this roll, saying: Why have you written upon it, saying, "The king of Bavel shall surely come and destroy this land and cause man and beast to cease from it"?
Therefore, so Havayah said concerning Yehoyakim the king of Yehudah; He shall have no one sitting on the throne of Dovid, and his corpse shall be cast to the heat by day and to the frost at night.

And I will visit upon him and upon his seed and upon his servants the punishment for their iniquity, and I will bring upon them and upon the inhabitants of Yerushalayim and upon the men of Yehudah all the evil that I spoke to them and which they did not heed.

And Yirmiyahu took another roll and gave it to Baruch the son of Neiriyah the scribe, and he wrote on it from the mouth of Yirmiyahu all the words of the book that Yehoyakim the king of Yehudah burnt with fire, and there were yet added to them many words like those.
And Tzidkiyahu the son of Yoshiyahu reigned as king instead of Konyahu the son of Yehoyakim, whom Nevuchadretzar the king of Bavel made king in the land of Yehudah.
And neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land hearkened to the words of Havayah which He had spoken through Yirmiyahu the prophet.
And King Tzidkiyahu sent Yehuchal the son of Shelemyahu and Tzefanyah the son of Maaseiyah the priest to Yirmiyahu the prophet, saying: "Pray now for us to Havayah our Elokim."
Now Yirmiyahu was coming and going among the people, and they did not put him into prison.
Now Paroh's army had left Mitzrayim, and the Kasdim who were besieging Yerushalayim heard news of them and withdrew from Yerushalayim.
And the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu the prophet, saying:
So Havayah Elokim said of Yisroel; So shall you say to the king of Yehudah who sent you to Me to inquire of Me; Behold, Paroh's army that has come out to aid you is returning to his land Mitzrayim.
And the Kasdim shall return and wage war on this city and capture it and burn it with fire.
So Havayah said: Deceive not yourselves, saying, "The Kasdim shall surely withdraw from us," for they shall not withdraw.
For if you smite the whole army of the Kasdim that fight against you, and but wounded men among them remain, each man shall rise in his tent and burn this city with fire.
And it came to pass when the army of the Kasdim withdrew from Yerushalayim because of Paroh's army,
that Yirmiyahu left Yerushalayim to go to the land of Binyamin to share land from there among the people.

And he was in the Binyamin Gate, and there was the captain of the guard, and his name was Yiriyah the son of Shelemyahu the son of Chananyah, and he seized Yirmiyahu the prophet, saying, "You are defecting to the Kasdim."
And Yirmiyahu said, "A lie! I am not defecting to the Kasdim." But he did not heed him, and Yiriyah seized Yirmiyahu and brought him to the officers.
And the officers were wroth with Yirmiyahu and they struck him, and they put him into the prison in the house of Yehonatan the scribe, for they had made it into a prison.
For Yirmiyahu had come to the dungeon and to the cells, and Yirmiyahu stayed there many days.

And King Tzidkiyahu sent and took him, and the king asked him secretly in his house, and he said, "Is there a word from Havayah?" And Yirmiyahu said, "There is." And he said, "You shall be given into the hands of the king of Bavel."
And Yirmiyahu said to King Tzidkiyahu, "What have I sinned against you and against your servants and against this people, that you have put me into the prison?
And where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, 'The king of Bavel shall not come upon you or upon this land'?
And now, please hearken, my master the king, may my supplication fall before you, and do not return me to the house of Yehonatan the scribe, and let me not die there."

And King Tzidkiyahu commanded, and they committed Yirmiyahu to the prison yard and he commanded to give him daily a loaf of bread from the street of the bakers until all the bread of the city was gone, and Yirmiyahu stayed in the prison yard.

And Shefatyah the son of Matan and Gedalyahu the son of Pashchur and Yehuchal the son of Shelemyahu and Pashchur the son of Malkiyah heard the words that Yirmiyahu was speaking to all the people, saying:
So Havayah said: Whoever stays in this city shall die by the sword, by famine, or by pestilence, and whoever goes out to the Kasdim shall live, and he shall have his life as a prey, and live.
So Havayah said: This city shall surely be given into the hands of the army of the king of Bavel, and he shall take it.

And the officers said to the king, "This man should be put to death now, since he weakens the hands of the men of war remaining in this city and the hands of all the people, to speak to them such words, for this man does not seek the welfare of this people but the harm."
And King Tzidkiyahu said, "Here he is in your hands, for the king cannot reply anything to you."

And they took Yirmiyahu and cast him into the pit of Malkiyah the king's son, that is in the prison yard, and they let Yirmiyahu down with ropes, and in the pit there was no water but mud, and Yirmiyahu sank into the mud.
And Eved-Melech the Kushi, an officer who was in the king's house, heard that they had put Yirmiyahu into the pit, and the king was sitting in the Binyamin gate.
And Eved-Melech went out of the king's house and spoke to the king, saying,

"My master the king, these men have done harm with all they have done to Yirmiyahu the prophet, let alone that they cast him into the pit. He would have died in his place because of the famine, for there is no more bread in the city."
And the king commanded Eved-Melech the Kushi, saying, "Take in your charge thirty men from here, and bring Yirmiyahu the prophet up from the pit while he has not yet died."

And Eved-Melech took the men in his charge and came to the king's house, under the treasury, and he took from there worn clouts and worn rags, and he let them down to Yirmiyahu into the pit with ropes.
And Eved-Melech the Kushi said to Yirmiyahu, "Now put the clouts and the rags under your armpits under the ropes," and Yirmiyahu did so.
And they pulled Yirmiyahu with the ropes, and they drew him up from the pit, and Yirmiyahu stayed in the prison yard.

And King Tzidkiyahu sent and took Yirmiyahu the prophet to him, to the third entrance, that was in the house of Havayah, and the king said to Yirmiyahu, "I ask you a word; do not conceal a word from me."
And Yirmiyahu said to Tzidkiyahu, "If I tell you, will you not put me to death? And if I advise you, you will not listen to me."

And King Tzidkiyahu swore to Yirmiyahu secretly, saying, "As Havayah lives who made for us this soul, I will neither put you to death nor will I deliver you into the hands of these men who seek your life."

And Yirmiyahu said to Tzidkiyahu, "So Havayah Elokim of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; If you go out to the officers of the king of Bavel, your soul shall live, and this city shall not be burnt with fire, and you and your household shall live.
But if you do not go out to the officers of the king of Bavel, this city shall be delivered into the hands of the Kasdim, and they shall burn it with fire, and you shall not escape from their hands."
And King Tzidkiyahu said to Yirmiyahu, "I fear the Yehudim who have defected to the Kasdim, lest they deliver me into their hands and mock me."
And Yirmiyahu said, "They shall not deliver you; hearken now to the voice of Havayah, that I speak to you, and it shall be good for you, and your soul shall live.
But if you refuse to go out, this is the thing that Havayah has shown me.

Behold, all the women who remained in the house of the king of Yehudah shall be taken out to the officers of the king of Bavel, and they shall say, 'Your cohorts have enticed you and prevailed over you. Your feet have sunk into the mire; they have turned back.'

And all your wives and your sons shall be brought out to the Kasdim, and you shall not escape from their hands, for you shall be seized by the hand of the king of Bavel, and this city you shall burn with fire."
And Tzidkiyahu said to Yirmiyahu, "Let no man know of these words, and you shall not die.

And when the officers hear that I spoke with you, and they come to you and say to you. 'Tell us now what you spoke to the king, do not conceal from us and we will not put you to death, and what did the king speak to you?'
You shall say to them, 'I presented my supplication before the king that he return me not to the house of Yehonatan to die there.' "
And all the officers came to Yirmiyahu and asked him, and he told them according to all these words that the king had commanded, and they left off speaking with him, for the matter was not reported.
And Yirmiyahu stayed in the prison yard until the day that Yerushalayim was taken, and he was there when Yerushalayim was taken.
In the ninth year of Tzidkiyahu the king of Yehudah, in the tenth month, Nevuchadretzar the king of Bavel and all his army came to Yerushalayim and besieged it.
In the eleventh year of Tzidkiyahu, in the fourth month on the ninth of the month, a breach was made in the city.

And all the officers of the king of Bavel came and sat in the middle gates Nergal-Saretzer, Samgar-Nevo, Sarsachim Rav-Saris, Nergal-Saretzer Rav-Mag, and all the rest of the officers of the king of Bavel.

And it came to pass when Tzidkiyahu the king of Yehudah and all the men of war saw them, that they fled and went out at night from the city by way of the king's garden by the gate between the two walls, and he went out by way of the Aravah.

And the army of the Kasdim pursued them, and they overtook Tzidkiyahu on the plains of Yericho, and they took him and brought him up to Nevuchadretzar the king of Bavel to Rivlah in the land of Chamas, and he called him to account.
And the king of Bavel slaughtered Tzidkiyahu's sons in Rivlah before his eye, and the king of Bavel slaughtered all the nobles of Yehudah.
And he blinded Tzidkiyahu's eyes, and he bound him with copper chains to bring him to Bavel.
And the king's palace and the houses of the people the Kasdim burnt with fire, and they demolished the walls of Yerushalayim.
And the rest of the people who remained in the city, and the defectors who had defected to him, and the rest of the remaining people, Nevuzaradan, the chief executioner, exiled to Bavel.
And the poor of the people who had nothing, Nevuzaradan the chief executioner left in the land of Yehudah, and he gave them vineyards and fields on that day.
And Nevuchadretzar the king of Bavel gave charge concerning Yirmiyahu in the custody of Nevuzaradan the chief executioner, saying,
"Take him and look after him and do no harm to him, but whatever he speaks to you, do so with him."
And he sent Nevuzaradan the chief executioner and Nevushazban Rav-Saris and Nergal-Saretzer Rav-Mag and all the officers of the king of Bavel.
And they sent and took Yirmiyahu from the prison yard and gave him over to Gedalyahu the son of Achikam the son of Shafan to take him out to the house, and he dwelt among the people.
And the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu when he was imprisoned in the prison yard, saying:

Go and say to Eved-Melech the Kushi, saying: So Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; Behold I bring My words upon this city for evil and not for good, and they shall be before you on that day.
And I will save you on that day, Havayah says, and you shall not be given into the hands of the men whom you fear.
For I will surely deliver you, and you shall not fall by the sword, and your life shall be to you for prey for you have trusted Me Havayah says.

The word that came to Yirmiyahu from Havayah after Nevuzaradan the chief executioner sent him away from Ramah when he took him and he was bound in fetters among the entire exile of Yerushalayim and Yehudah who were exiled to Bavel.
And the chief executioner took Yirmiyahu and said to him, "The Havayah your Elokim spoke this evil upon this place.
And Havayah has brought and performed as He spoke, for you sinned against Havayah, and you did not hearken to His voice, and this thing has come upon you.

And now, behold I have released you today from the fetters that are on your hands; if it pleases you to come with me to Bavel, come, and I will look after you, and if it does not please you to come with me to Bavel, refrain. See, the whole land is before you; wherever it seems good and right to you to go, go there."

But he would still not return, "So return to Gedalyahu the son of Achikam the son of Shafan, whom the king of Bavel has appointed in the cities of Yehudah, and stay with him amidst the people, or go wherever it seems right to you to go," and the chief executioner gave him an allowance and a present and sent him away.
And Yirmiyahu came to Gedalyahu the son of Achikam, to Mitzpah, and he lived with him amidst the people remaining in the land.

And all the officers of the armies that were in the field heard, they and their men that the king of Bavel had appointed Gedalyahu the son of Achikam in the land, and that he had appointed with him men, women, and children, and of the poor of the land, of those who were not exiled to Bavel.

And they came to Gedalyahu to Mitzpah, and Yishmael the son of Netanyahu and Yochanan and Yehonatan the sons of Kareach and Serayah the son of Tanchumes and the sons of Eifai the Netofasi and Yezanyah the son of the Maachasi, they and their men.
And Gedalyahu the son of Achikam the son of Shafan swore to them and to their men, saying, "Fear not to serve the Kasdim. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Bavel, and it will go well with you.

And I, behold I dwell in Mitzpah to stand before the Kasdim who will come to us, and you gather wine and dried figs and oil and put them into your vessels and dwell in your cities, which you have taken.

And also, all the Yehudim who were in Moav and among the children of Ammon and in Edom and who were in all the lands, heard that the king of Bavel had given Yehudah a remnant and that he had appointed over them Gedalyahu the son of Achikam the son of Shafan.
And all the Yehudim returned from all the places they had been driven, and they came to the land of Yehudah to Gedalyahu to Mitzpah, and they gathered very much wine and dried figs.
And Yochanan the son of Kareach and all the officers of the armies who were in the field, came to Gedalyahu to Mitzpah.
And they said to him, "Do you know that Baalis the king of the children of Ammon sent Yishmael the son of Netanyahu to assassinate you?" But Gedalyahu the son of Achikam did not believe them.

And Yochanan the son of Kareach said to Gedalyahu secretly, in Mitzpah, saying, "Let me go now and I will slay Yishmael the son of Netanyahu, and no one shall know. Why should he put you to death, and all the Yehudim gathered to you scatter, and the remnant of Yehudah be lost?"
And Gedalyahu the son of Achikam said to Yochanan the son of Kareach, "Do not do this thing for you speak falsely about Yishmael."

And it came to pass in the seventh month, that Yishmael the son of Netanyahu the son of Elishama of royal descent and officers of the king and ten men with him, came to Gedalyahu the son of Achikam, to Mitzpah, and they ate bread there together in Mitzpah.

And Yishmael the son of Netanyahu and the ten men who were with him arose and smote Gedalyahu the son of Achikam the son of Shafan, with the sword, and he slew him, whom the king of Bavel had appointed in the land,
and all the Yehudim who were with him, with Gedalyahu in Mitzpah, and the Kasdim who were found there, the men of war, Yishmael smote.
