And it came about on the second day of his slaying Gedalyahu — and no one knew

that men came from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Shomron, eighty men, with shaven beards and rent garments and having cut themselves, with a meal-offering and frankincense in their hands, to bring to the house of Havayah.
And Yishmael the son of Netanyahu came out toward them from Mitzpah, walking and weeping, and it came about when he met them, that he said to them, "Come to Gedalyahu the son of Achikam."
And it came to pass when they came into the midst of the city, that Yishmael the son of Netanyahu slew them into the pit, he and the men who were with him.

And ten men were found among them, and they said to Yishmael, "Do not slay us, for we have stores in the field; wheat and barley and oil and honey." And he refrained and did not slay them among their brothers.

Now the pit into which Yishmael had cast all the corpses of the men whom he had slain because of Gedalyahu — that was the one that King Asa had made because of Ba'asha, king of Yisroel. That one Yishmael the son of Netanyahu filled with corpses.

And Yishmael captured all the remnant of the people that was in Mitzpah, the daughters of the king and all the people remaining in Mitzpah, whom Nevuzaradan the chief executioner had committed to Gedalyahu the son of Achikam, and Yishmael the son of Netanyahu captured them and went to cross over to the children of Ammon.
And Yochanan the son of Kareach and all the officers of the armies who were with him heard all the evil that Yishmael the son of Netanyahu had done.
And they took all the men and went to fight with Yishmael the son of Netanyahu, and they found him by the great waters that are in Givon.
And it came to pass when all the people who were with Yishmael saw Yochanan the son of Kareach and all the officers of the armies who were with him, they rejoiced.
And all the people whom Yishmael had captured from Mitzpah turned around, and they returned and went to Yochanan the son of Kareach.
And Yishmael the son of Netanyahu fled with eight men from before Yochanan and went to the children of Ammon.

And Yochanan the son of Kareach and all the officers of the armies who were with him took the entire remnant of the people that he had recovered from Yishmael the son of Netanyahu from Mitzpah after he had slain Gedalyahu the son of Achikam, the men, even the men of war, and the women and children and the officers whom he had brought back from Givon.
And they went and dwelt in Geirus Kimham that is next to Beis Lechem, to go to come to Mitzrayim,
because of the Kasdim, for they feared them, for Yishmael the son of Netanyahu had slain Gedalyahu the son of Achikam, whom the king of Bavel had appointed in the land.
And all the officers of the armies and Yochanan the son of Kareach and Yezanyah the son of Hoshayah and all the people from the smallest to the greatest, came near.

And they said to Yirmiyahu the prophet, "Let our supplication now fall before you, and pray in our behalf to Havayah your Elokim on behalf of all this remnant, for we remain few out of many, as your eyes see us.
And then let Havayah your Elokim tell the way we should go and the thing we should do.

And Yirmiyahu the prophet said to them, "I have heard you. Behold I will pray to Havayah your Elokim according to your words, and it will come to pass that whatever Havayah answers you I will tell you; I will not withhold anything from you."
And they said to Yirmiyahu, "May Havayah be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not do according to the entire matter that Havayah your Elokim shall send you to us.
Whether good or bad, we will hearken to the voice of Havayah our Elokim, to Whom we are sending you, in order that it be good for us, for we will hearken to the voice of Havayah our Elokim.
And it came to pass at the end of ten days that the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu.
And he called out to Yochanan the son of Kareach and to all the officers of the armies that were with him, both great and small.
And he said to them: So Havayah Elokim said of Yisroel, to Whom you have sent me to present your supplication before Him.
If you dwell in this land, I will build you up and I will not pluck you up, for I have repented of the evil that I have done to you.
Fear not the king of Bavel whom you fear; fear it not, Havayah says, for I am with you to redeem you and to save you from his hand.
And I will give you mercy, and he shall have mercy on you, and he shall return you to your land.
But if you say, "We will not dwell in this land, not to hearken to the voice of Havayah your Elokim,
saying, 'No, but we will come to the land of Mitzrayim, where we will neither see war not hear the sound of the horn, nor be hungry for bread, and there we will dwell.' "
And now, therefore, hearken to the word of Havayah, O remnant of Yehudah, so Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; If you direct your faces to come to Mitzrayim and you come to dwell there,
the sword that you fear will overtake you there in the land of Mitzrayim, and the famine that you are worried about shall overtake you there in Mitzrayim, and there you shall die.

And so shall it be with all the men who directed their faces to Mitzrayim to sojourn there; they shall die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence, and they shall have neither survivor nor refugee because of the evil that I am bringing upon them.

For so Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; As My wrath and My fury have been poured out upon the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, so shall My wrath and My fury be poured out upon you when you come to Mitzrayim, and you shall be for an oath and for a bewilderment and for a curse and for a reproach, and you shall no longer see this place.
The Havayah spoke concerning you, O remnant of Yehudah; do not come to Mitzrayim. You shall know certainly that I have warned you today.

For you have wilfully deceived, for you have sent me to Havayah your Elokim, saying, "Pray for us to Havayah our Elokim, and according to all that Havayah our Elokim shall say, so tell us, and we will do it."
And I told you today, but you did not hearken to the voice of Havayah your Elokim or to all that He sent me to you.
And now, you shall certainly know that you shall die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence in the place where you desired to sojourn.
And it came to pass when Yirmiyahu finished speaking to all the people all the words of Havayah their Elokim which Havayah their Elokim had sent him to them, all these words,

then said Azaryah the son of Hoshayah and Yochanan the son of Kareach and all the wilfully wicked people, saying to Yirmiyahu, "You speak falsely; Havayah our Elokim did not send you to say, 'You shall not come to Mitzrayim to sojourn there.'
But Baruch the son of Neiriyah incites you against us, in order to deliver us into the hands of the Kasdim to put us to death and to exile us to Bavel."
And Yochanan the son of Kareach and all the officers of the armies and all the people did not hearken to the voice of Havayah to dwell in the land of Yehudah.

And Yochanan the son of Kareach and all the officers of the armies took all the remnant of Yehudah that had returned from all the nations where they had been driven, to sojourn in the land of Yehudah,

the men and the women and the children and the king's daughters and all the people whom Nevuzaradan the chief executioner had left with Gedalyahu the son of Achikam the son of Shafan, and Yirmiyahu the prophet and Baruch the son of Neiriyah.
And they came to the land of Mitzrayim, for they did not hearken to the voice of Havayah, and they came to Tachpanches.
And the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu in Tachpanches, saying:
Take in your hand large stones and hide them in the mortar in the framework, which is at the entrance of Paroh's house in Tachpanches, before the eyes of Yehudi men.

And you shall say to them: So Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; Behold I am sending, and I will take Nevuchadretzar the king of Bavel, My servant, and I will put his throne over these stones which I have hidden, and he shall spread his royal pavilion over them.
And he shall come and smite the land of Mitzrayim, those who are for death, for death, and those who are for captivity, for captivity, and those who are for the sword, for the sword.

And I will ignite a fire in the houses of the gods of Mitzrayim, and he shall burn them and capture them, and he shall wrap up the land of Mitzrayim as a shepherd wraps up his garment, and he shall leave there in peace.
And he shall break the monuments of Beis-Shemesh which is in the land of Mitzrayim, and the houses of the gods of Mitzrayim he shall burn with fire.
The word that came to Yirmiyahu concerning all the Yehudim dwelling in the land of Mitzrayim, those dwelling in Migdol and in Tachpanches and in Nof and in the land of Patros, saying:

So Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; You saw all the evil that I brought upon Yerushalayim and upon all the cities of Yehudah, and behold, they are waste, and there are no inhabitants in them,
because of their evil, which they did to provoke Me, to go to burn incense to worship other gods, which they did not know, neither did you nor your forefathers.
And I sent to you all My servants the prophets, sending them betimes, saying: Now do not do this abominable thing which I hate.
But they did not hearken, nor did they incline their ears to repent of their evil, not to burn incense to other gods.
And My anger and My fury were poured out, and it burnt in the cities of Yehudah and in the streets of Yerushalayim, and they have become waste and desolate as this day.

And now, so Havayah Elokim of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; Why do you do this great evil to your souls, to cut off from you man and woman, child and suckling from the midst of Yehudah, not to leave over a remnant for yourselves,

to provoke Me with the deeds of your hands, to burn incense to other gods in the land of Mitzrayim where you are coming to sojourn, in order to cut yourselves off and in order for you to become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth.

Have you forgotten the evils of your forefathers and the evils of the kings of Yehudah and the evils of his wives and the evils of your wives, that they did in the land of Yehudah and in the streets of Yerushalayim?
They were not crushed until this day, and they did not fear, and they did not walk in My Law and in My statutes that I placed before you and before your forefathers.
Therefore, so Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; Behold I direct My face against you for evil and to cut off all of Yehudah.

And I will take the remnant of Yehudah that directed their faces to come to the land of Mitzrayim to sojourn there, and all shall be consumed; in the land of Mitzrayim they shall fall, by the sword and by famine they shall be consumed, both great and small shall die by the sword and by famine, and they shall be for an oath, for bewilderment, and for a curse and a reproach.
And I will visit upon those dwelling in the land of Mitzrayim as I visited upon Yerushalayim, by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence.

There shall be neither fugitive nor survivor to the remnant of Yehudah coming to sojourn there in the land of Mitzrayim and to return to the land of Yehudah, for they mislead themselves to return to dwell there, for only fugitives shall return.

And all the men who knew that their wives burned incense to other gods and all the women standing in a great assembly, and all the people dwelling in the land of Mitzrayim, in Patros, answered Yirmiyahu, saying,
"The word that you spoke to us in the name of Havayah, we will not hearken to you.

But we will do everything that has emanated from our mouth, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and to pour libations to her, as we did, we, our forefathers, our kings, and our princes, in the cities of Yehudah and in the streets of Yerushalayim, and we were sated with bread, and we were well, and we saw no evil.
But since we stopped burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring libations to her, we lack everything, and we have been consumed by the sword and by famine.
And when we burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour libations to her, did we make her cakes in her image without our husbands, or pour out libations to her?"
And Yirmiyahu said to all the people, to the men, to the women, and to all the people who answered him a word, saying,

"The incense that you burnt in the cities of Yehudah and in the streets of Yerushalayim, you and your forefathers, your kings and your princes, and the people of the land, did not Havayah remember them and did it not enter His heart?

And He could no longer bear because of the evil of your deeds, because of the abominations that you committed, and your land became waste and desolation and a curse, without an inhabitant as this day.

Because you burnt incense and because you sinned against Havayah, and you did not hearken to the voice of Havayah, and you did not walk in His Law and in His statutes and in His testimonies; therefore, this evil has befallen you as of this day."
And Yirmiyahu said to all the people and to all the women: Hearken to the word of Havayah, all of Yehudah that is in the land of Mitzrayim.

So Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel, saying: You and your wives; as you have spoken with your mouth, so have you fulfilled with your hands, saying, "We will surely execute our vows, as we have vowed to burn incense to the queen of heaven and to pour libations to her." You shall surely fulfill your vows and you shall surely execute your vows.

Therefore, hearken to the word of Havayah, all of Yehudah dwelling in the land of Mitzrayim; Behold, I have sworn by My great name, Havayah said, that My name shall no longer be called by the mouth of any man of Yehudah, saying, "As Havayah Elokim lives," throughout the land of Mitzrayim.
Behold, I visit upon them for evil and not for good, and every man of Yehudah who is in the land of Mitzrayim shall be consumed by the sword, and by famine until they are completely destroyed.

And fugitives of the sword who shall return from the land of Mitzrayim to the land of Yehudah shall be few in number, and all the remnant of Yehudah that came to the land of Mitzrayim to sojourn there shall know whose word shall stand, whether Mine or theirs.
And this shall be to you the sign, Havayah says, that I will visit upon you in this place, in order that you know that My words shall surely stand against you for evil.

So Havayah said: Behold I deliver Paroh Chafra, the king of Mitzrayim, into the hands of his enemies and into the hands of those who seek his life, as I delivered Tzidkiyahu, the king of Yehudah, into the hands of Nevuchadretzar, the king of Bavel, his enemy and the one who sought his life.

The word that Yirmiyahu the prophet spoke to Baruch the son of Neiriyah when he wrote these words on a scroll from the mouth of Yirmiyahu in the fourth year of Yehoyakim the son of Yoshiyahu, the king of Yehudah, saying:
So Havayah Elokim said of Yisroel concerning you, Baruch:
You said, "Woe is to me now, for Havayah has added grief to my pain. I have become weary with my sighing, but I have found no rest."
So shall you say to him, So Havayah said: Behold what I have built I will tear down, and what I planted I will uproot, and it is all the land.
And you seek great things for yourself? Do not seek, for behold I am bringing evil upon all flesh, Havayah says, and I will give you your soul as prey in all the places where you will go.
That the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu the prophet concerning the nations.

Concerning Mitzrayim, concerning the army of Paroh-Necho, the king of Mitzrayim which was on the Peras in Karkemish, whom Nevuchadretzar king of Bavel smote in the fourth year of Yehoyakim the son of Yoshiyahu the king of Yehudah.
Make ready shield and buckler and draw near to battle.
Harness the steeds, and mount, you riders, and stand with helmets, polish the spears, don the coats of mail.
Why do I see them breaking retreating, and their heroes are crushed and have fled and were not freed? There is terror all around, Havayah says.
The swift shall not flee, neither shall the mighty man escape; northward by the Peras River, they stumbled and fell.
Who is this that would come up like the Yeor; like the rivers its waters would toss themselves?
Mitzrayim would come up like the Yeor, and like the rivers, the water would toss itself, and he said, "I will go up, I will cover the land, I will destroy the city and those who dwell therein.
Ascend, you horses, and rush madly you chariots, and let the mighty men come forth, Kush and Put, the shield bearers, and the Ludim who grasp and bend the bow.

And that day shall be for Havayah Elokim of Hosts a day of vengeance, to avenge Himself against His adversaries, and the sword shall consume and shall be sated, and its thirst shall be quenched by their blood, for Havayah Elokim of Hosts shall have a massacre in the north land by the Peras River.
Go up to Gilad and take balm, O virgin daughter of Mitzrayim; in vain have you increased medicines, you have no cure.
Nations have heard your disgrace, and your cry has filled the earth, for a mighty man has stumbled upon a mighty man; together they have both fallen."
The word that Havayah spoke to Yirmiyahu the prophet, concerning the coming of Nevuchadretzar king of Bavel to smite the land of Mitzrayim.
Proclaim it in Mitzrayim and let it be heard in Migdol, and let it be heard in Nof and in Tachpanches, say, "Stand fast and prepare yourself, for the sword has devoured round about you."
Why have your mighty men been swept away? None of them stood, for Havayah pushed him down.
He made many stumbling blocks, yea, they joined one another, and they said, "Arise, and let us return to our own people and to the land of our birth, before the oppressing sword."
There they called out, "Paroh, king of Mitzrayim, who made a lot of noise, has allowed the appointed time to pass by!"
As long as I live, says the King, Whose name is Havayah of Hosts, that as sure as Tavor is among the mountains, and Karmel is by the sea, it shall come about.
O you daughter who lives in Mitzrayim, make for yourself equipment for exile, for Nof shall become waste and desolate without an inhabitant.
Mitzrayim was a fair heifer; destruction from the north is coming, yea it is coming!

Also her princes who are in her midst are like fattened calves, for they too turn around and flee together, they do not hold their ground, for the day of their calamity has come upon them, the time of their visitation.
Its voice shall go like that of the snake, for they will march with an army and will come against her with axes as if they were hewers of wood.
They will cut down her forest, Havayah says, for they are innumerable, for they are more numerous than locusts and they are uncountable.
The daughter of Mitzrayim has been put to shame; she has been delivered into the hands of the people of the north.

The Havayah of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisroel has said: Lo I will visit upon Amon of No and upon Paroh and upon Mitzrayim, and upon their gods and upon their kings, both upon Paroh and upon those who put their trust in him.

And I will deliver them into the hands of those who seek their lives and into the hands of Nevuchadretzar, king of Bavel, and into the hands of his servants — and after that it will be inhabited again as in the days of old, Havayah says.

You fear not, O Yackov My servant, and be not dismayed, O Yisroel! for behold, I will redeem you from afar and your children from the land of their captivity, and Yackov shall return and be quiet and at ease, and there shall be none who disturb his rest.

You fear not, My servant Yackov, Havayah says, for I am with you, for I will make a full end of all the nations where I have driven you, but of you I will not make a full end, but I will chastise you justly, and I will not completely destroy you.
That the word of Havayah came to Yirmiyahu the prophet concerning the Pelishtim before Paroh smote Azah.

So Havayah said: Behold water is coming up from the north, and it shall become a flooding stream and will inundate a land and the fullness thereof, a city and those who dwell therein, and the people shall cry out, and all the inhabitants of the land shall wail.
From the sound of the stamping of the hoofs of his mighty ones, from the noise of his chariots, the stirring of his wheels; fathers did not turn to sons out of the feebleness of their hands,
because of the day that is coming to plunder all the Pelishtim, to cut off from Tzor and Tzidon every surviving helper, for Havayah plunders the Pelishtim, the remnant of the island of Caphtor.
Baldness has come to Azah, Ashkelon has become a waste, yea the remnant of their valley; how long will you tear your flesh?
Ho! Sword of Havayah, how long will you not be silent'? Go into your sheath, rest and be silent.
How shall you be silent when Havayah commanded it? To Ashkelon and to the sea coast, there He appointed it.
Concerning Moav. So Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; Woe to Nevo for it is spoiled; Kiryatayim is shamed, it is taken; Misgav is shamed and broken.
The praise of Moav is no more; in Cheshbon they planned harm to her; Let us go and cut her off from being a nation. Also, Madmen, you shall be a waste; the sword shall follow you.
A voice of a cry shall be heard from Choronayim; plunder and great destruction.
Moav is broken; her youths have let a cry be heard.
The ascent of Luchis with weeping shall he ascend, yea weeping, for in the descent of Choronayim the adversaries heard a cry of destruction.
Flee, save your lives, and you shall be like Aro'er in the desert.
For, since you relied on your deeds and on your treasures, you too shall be taken, and Kemosh shall go forth into exile, his priests and his princes together.
And the spoiler shall come to every city, and no city shall escape, and the valley shall be lost and the plain destroyed, as Havayah has said.
Give wings to Moav for she shall fly away, and her cities shall become waste, without anyone dwelling in them.
Cursed be he who performs Havayah's work deceitfully, and cursed be he who withholds his sword from blood.

Moav has been at ease since his youth, and he is settled on his lees, and he has not been poured from one vessel to another vessel, and he has not gone into exile; therefore, its flavor remained therein, and its bouquet did not change.
Therefore, behold days are coming, Havayah says, and I will send men to pour him out and they shall pour him out, and they shall empty his vessels and smash his jars.
And Moav shall be ashamed of Kemosh, as the house of Yisroel was ashamed of Beis-El, their reliance.
How do you say, "We are mighty men, and valiant men for war?"
Moav has been plundered, and her cities have been laid waste, and the choicest of their young men have gone down to the slaughter, says the King, Havayah of Hosts is His name.
The destruction of Moav is near to come, and his evil has hastened exceedingly.
Lament for them, all those around them, and all who know their name, say: How has the staff of strength been broken, the rod of glory?
Come down from glory and sit in thirst, O daughter who dwells in Divon, for the spoiler of Moav has marched upon you, he has destroyed your fortresses.
Stand by the road and look, O dweller of Aro'er, ask those who have fled and escaped, tell what has transpired.
Moav is ashamed for it is broken; wail and cry, tell in Arnon that Moav has been spoiled.
And judgment has come to the land of the plain, to Cholon and to Yahatz and to Meifaas.
and to Divon and to Nevo and to Beis-Divlatayim,
and to Kiryatayim and to Beis-Gamul and to Beis-Meon,
and to Keryos and to Batzrah and to all the cities of the land of Moav, both far and near.
The horn of Moav has been cut off, and his arm is broken, Havayah says.
Make him drunk, for he has magnified himself against Havayah, and Moav shall wallow in his vomit and he too shall become a derision.
For was not Yisroel a derision to you? Was he found among thieves, that whenever you speak of him you shake your head?
Leave the cities and dwell in the rock, you inhabitants of Moav, and be like a dove, that nests in the sides of the mouth of a pit.
We have heard the pride of Moav, very proud, his loftiness and his pride and his haughtiness, and the arrogance of his heart.
I know, Havayah says, his wrath, and it is not so, his mighty men have not dealt properly.
Therefore, I wail for Moav, and for all of Moav I will cry; for the people of Kir-Cheres they shall moan.

From the weeping of Yazer I will weep for you, O grape vine of Sivmah; your tendrils have crossed the sea, they reached the sea of Yazer; upon your dried figs and upon your vintage the spoiler has fallen.

And joy and jubilation shall be taken away from the fruitful field and from the land of Moav, and I will cause the wine to cease from the pits. No one shall tread with shouting; The shouting shall be no shouting.
From the cry of Cheshbon until Elaleh, they let out their voice as far as Yahatz, from Tzoar until Choronayim, O third-born heifer, for also the waters of Nimrim shall become wastelands.
And I will cause to cease from Moav, Havayah says, one who offers up sacrifices on the high places and who burns incense to his gods.
Therefore, my heart shall stir for Moav like flutes, and my heart shall stir for the men of Kir-Cheres like flutes; because they dealt haughtily,
For every head is bald and every beard clipped; on all hands are scratches, and on the loins sackcloth.
On all the roofs of Moav and in her broad places, there is lamentation everywhere, for I have broken Moav like a vessel that has no use, Havayah says.
Wail, "How was she dismayed? How did Moav turn its back?" They were shamed, and Moav became a derision and a dismay to all its surroundings.
For so Havayah said: Behold, like an eagle he shall soar and spread out his wings upon Moav.
Keryos has been taken, and the fortresses have been seized; and the heart of the mighty men of Moav shall be on that day like the heart of a woman travailing.
And Moav shall be destroyed from being a people, for they magnified themselves against Havayah.
Fright and a pit and a snare shall be upon you, O dweller of Moav, Havayah says.
Whoever flees the fright shall fall into the pit, and whoever ascends from the pit shall be caught in the snare, for I will bring to her, to Moav the year of their visitation, Havayah says.

In the shadow of Cheshbon, those who were fleeing stood for lack of strength, for a fire emanated from Cheshbon and a flame from the city of Sichon, and it consumed the corner of Moav and the crown of the head of the tumultuous ones.
Woe to you, Moav, the people of Kemosh is lost, for your sons have been taken into captivity and your daughters into captivity.
And I will return the captivity of Moav at the end of days, Havayah says. Until here is the judgment of Moav.
Concerning the children of Ammon. So Havayah said: Has Yisroel no sons? Has he no heir? Why has Malkam taken possession of Gad, and his people have settled his cities?

Therefore, behold days are coming, Havayah says, and I will cause an alarm of war to be heard against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and it shall become a desolate mound, and its villages shall be burnt with fire, and Yisroel shall possess those who have possessed their possessions, Havayah says.

Wail, O Cheshbon, for Ai has been spoiled, cry out, O villages of Rabbah, gird yourselves with sackcloth, lament and mobilize in companies, for Malkam shall go into exile, his priests and his princes together.
Why do you boast about the valleys? Your valley is flowing, O backsliding daughter, who depends on her treasures, saying, "Who shall come to me?"
Behold I bring fright upon you, Havayah Elokim of Hosts says, from all those around you, and you shall be driven, each man forward, and no one shall take in the wanderer.
And afterwards, I will return the captivity of the children of Ammon, Havayah says.
Concerning Edom, So Havayah of Hosts said: Is there no more wisdom in the south? Counsel is lost from the sons, their wisdom has spoiled.
Flee! Clear out! Dwell deep, O dwellers of Dedan, for the misfortune of Eisav have I brought upon him, the times I have visited upon him.
If vintagers have come upon you, will they not leave over gleaning grapes? If thieves at night, they destroy until they have enough.
For I exposed Eisav, I revealed his hidden places, and he could not hide; his seed, his brothers, and his neighbors were spoiled, and he is not here.
Leave your orphans, I will sustain them, and your widows shall trust in Me.
For so Havayah said: Behold, if those who did not deserve to drink the cup nevertheless shall drink; should you then be cleared? You shall not be cleared, but you shall surely drink.
For by Myself have I sworn, Havayah says, that Batzrah shall become desolation, reproach, waste, and a curse, and all her cities shall become perpetual wastelands.
I have heard tidings from Havayah, and an emissary is sent among the nations: Assemble and come upon her, and arise for war!
For, behold, I have made you small among the nations, despised among man.

Your hastiness has enticed you, the wickedness of your heart, you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, who hold the height of the hill; if you raise your nest like an eagle, from there will I bring you down, Havayah says.
And Edom shall become a desolation; whoever passes by her shall be astonished and shall hiss at all her plagues.
Like the overturning of Sedom and Amorah and her neighbors, Havayah said, no man shall dwell there, and no man shall sojourn there.

Behold, as a lion that ascends from the heights of the Yarden to a strong dwelling place, for I will bring the moment when I will hasten him away from her, and he who is chosen I will appoint to her, for who is like Me and who will appoint Me a time, and who is a shepherd who will stand before Me?

Therefore, hearken to the counsel of Havayah, which He advised concerning Edom, and His plans that He planned concerning the dwellers of the south, if the young of the flock will not drag them, if He will not make desolate their dwellings with them.
From the sound of their fall, the earth quaked; a cry whose sound was heard in the Yam Suf.
Behold like an eagle he shall ascend and soar, and he shall spread his wings over Batzrah, and the heart of the mighty men of Edom on that day shall be like the heart of a travailing woman.
Concerning Damesek, Chamas and Arpad are shamed for they have heard bad news, they melted; there is worry in the sea, it cannot be quiet.
Damesek has become feeble, she has turned to flee, and trembling has seized her: distress and pangs seized her like a woman in confinement.
"How was the city of praise not fortified, the city of my joy?"
Therefore, her youths shall fall in her broad places, and all her warriors shall be destroyed on that day, Havayah of Hosts says.
And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damesek, and it shall consume the palaces of the Ben-Hadad.
Concerning Keidar and concerning the kingdoms of Chatzor, which Nevuchadretzar the king of Bavel smote. So Havayah said: Go up to Keidar and spoil the children of the east.
Their tents and their flocks they shall take, their curtains and all their utensils and their camels they shall take for themselves, and they shall call upon them a terror on every side.
Flee, wander far off, dwell deep, inhabitants of Keidar, Havayah says, for Nevuchadretzar the king of Bavel has taken counsel against you and has devised a plot against you.
"Rise and go up to a peaceful nation, dwelling confidently," Havayah says; he has neither doors nor bars, they dwell alone.

And their camels shall be for a prey and the multitude of their cattle for spoil, and I will scatter them in all directions, cast to the ends, and from all its sides I will bring their misfortune, Havayah says.
And Chatzor shall become a habitat of jackals, desolate to eternity; neither shall any man dwell there nor shall any man sojourn therein.
The word of Havayah that came to Yirmiyahu the prophet concerning Eilam at the beginning of the reign of Tzidkiyahu the king of Yehudah, saying:
So Havayah of Hosts said: Behold I am breaking the bow of Eilam, the chief of their might.
And I will bring against Eilam four winds from the four ends of the heavens, and I will scatter them to all these winds, and there shall be no nation where the exiles of Eilam shall not come.

And I will break Eilam before their enemies and before those who seek their lives, and I will bring upon them evil — the kindling of My wrath, Havayah says, and I will send the sword after them until I completely destroy them.
And I will place My throne in Eilam and I will destroy from there a king and princes, Havayah says.
And it shall be at the end of days, that I will return the captivity of Eilam, Havayah says.
The word that Havayah spoke concerning Bavel, concerning the land of the Kasdim, by Yirmiyahu the prophet.

Tell among the nations and let it be heard and raise a standard; let them hear and do not hide it. Say, "Bavel has been taken, Bel has been shamed, Merodach is dismayed, her images have been shamed, her idols have been dismayed.
For a nation has marched against her from the north; he shall make her land a desolation, and no one shall dwell therein; both man and beast have wandered, yea they have gone.
In those days and in that time, Havayah says, the children of Yisroel shall come, they and the children of Yehudah together; they shall go along weeping, and they shall seek Havayah their Elokim.
They shall inquire of Tziyon; their faces are directed hitherward. "Come and join Havayah with an everlasting covenant that shall not be forgotten."
My people were lost sheep, their shepherds caused them to stray, to the mountains they led them astray; from mountain to hill they went, they forgot their resting place.
All who found them devoured them, and their adversaries said, "We are not to blame because they sinned against Havayah, the habitation of justice and the hope of their forefathers — Havayah."
Wander out of Bavel and go out of the land of the Kasdim, and be like the he-goats before the flocks.

For behold I am arousing and bringing up upon Bavel an alliance of great nations from the north land, and they shall set themselves in array against her, from there she shall be taken; his arrows are like those of a mighty man who bereaves, it shall not return empty.
And the land of the Kasdim shall become a prey; all who prey upon it shall be sated, Havayah says.
As you rejoice, as you jubilate, O spoilers of My heritage, as you become fat like a threshing heifer, and you neigh as strong horses,
your mother has been exceedingly shamed, she who bore you has been embarrassed; behold the end of the nations is desert, wasteland, and a barren plain.
Because of the wrath of Havayah, she shall not be inhabited, and all of her shall be desolate; whoever passes by Bavel shall be amazed and hiss about all her plagues.
Set yourselves in array against Bavel all around, all you who bend the bow, shoot at her, spare no arrow, for she has sinned against Havayah.
Shout against her all around; she gave her hand, her foundations have fallen, her walls are torn down, for it is Havayah's vengeance; wreak vengeance upon her: as she did, do to her.
Cut off a sower from Bavel and one who grasps a sickle at the time of harvest; because of the intoxicating sword, every man shall turn to his people, and every man shall flee to his land.
A scattered sheep is Yisroel which lions have driven away. First the king of Ashur devoured him, and this last one broke his bones, Nevuchadretzar the king of Bavel.
Therefore, so Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; Behold I visit retribution upon the king of Bavel and upon his land, as I visited upon the king of Ashur.
And I will return Yisroel to his dwelling and he shall pasture in the Karmel and the Bashan, and in Mount Efraim and Gilad shall his soul be sated.

In those days and at that time, Havayah says, the iniquity of Yisroel shall be sought, but it shall not be there, and the sins of Yehudah, but they shall not be found, for I will forgive those I leave over.
Upon the rebellious land, march upon her, and upon the inhabitants of Pekod; slay with the sword and utterly destroy after them, Havayah says, and do according to all that I have commanded you.
The sound of war is in the land and great destruction.
How is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder and broken? How has Bavel become a desolation among the nations?
I laid a snare for you, and you were also taken, O Bavel, and you were unaware; you were discovered and you were also seized, for you have stricken against Havayah.
The Havayah has opened his treasury and has taken out the weapons of His fury, for Havayah Elokim has work in the land of the Kasdim.
Come against her from the border, open her gates, thresh her like stacks of grain and utterly destroy her: let her have no remnant.
Slay all her bulls with the sword, let them go down to the slaughter; woe is to them for their day has come, the time of their visitation.
Hearken to those fleeing and escaping from the land of Bavel to tell in Tziyon the vengeance of Havayah our Elokim, the vengeance of His Temple.

Gather archers against Bavel, all those who bend the bow, encamp against her all around. Let her have no escape. Recompense her according to her deed; according to all that she has done, do to her, for she has dealt wickedly with Havayah, with the Holy One of Yisroel.
Therefore, her youths shall fall in her broad places, and all her warriors they shall be cut off on that day, Havayah says.
Behold I am against you, O man of wickedness, Havayah Elokim of Hosts says, for your day has come, the time I visit retribution upon you.
And the man of wickedness shall stumble and fall, and he shall have no one to raise him up, and I will kindle fire in his cities, and it shall consume all those around him.
So Havayah of Hosts said: The children of Yisroel and the children of Yehudah are plundered together, and all their captors have held onto them, they have refused to release them.
Their Redeemer is mighty; Havayah of Hosts is His name, He shall surely plead their cause, in order to give rest to the earth and unrest to the inhabitants of Bavel.
A sword is upon the Kasdim, Havayah says, and upon the inhabitants of Bavel and upon her princes and upon her wise men.
A sword is upon the imposters and they shall become foolish; a sword is upon her mighty men, and they shall become dismayed.
A sword is upon his horses and upon his chariots and upon all the allies who are in her midst, and they shall become like women; a sword is upon her treasuries, and they shall be spoiled.
A drought is upon her waters, and they shall dry up, for it is a land of graven images, and they are mad upon things of horror.
Therefore, martens shall dwell with cats, and ostriches shall dwell therein, and it shall never again be settled until eternity, neither shall it be inhabited from generation to generation.
Like Elokim's overturning Sedom and Amorah and her neighbors, Havayah says, no man shall dwell there, and no man shall sojourn therein.
Behold a people is coming from the north, and a great nation and great kings shall be aroused from the ends of the earth.
They grasp bow and spear; they are cruel, having no mercy; their voice is like the roaring sea, and they ride on steeds, arrayed like a man for war, against you, O daughter of Bavel.
The king of Bavel has heard the report of them, and his hands have become feeble; distress has grasped him, pangs like a woman in confinement.

Behold, as a lion that ascends from the heights of the Yarden to a strong dwelling, when I bring the moment that I will hasten them over her, for who is like Me and who will appoint Me a time, and who is a shepherd who will stand before Me?

Therefore, hearken to the counsel of Havayah, which He advised Bavel, and His plans that He planned concerning the land of the Kasdim, if the young of the flock will not drag them, if He will not make desolate their dwelling with them.
From the report that Bavel was taken, the earth quaked, and a cry was heard among the nations.
So Havayah said: Behold I arouse against Bavel and against the inhabitants of Lev-Kamai, the desire of a destroyer.
And I will send against Bavel foreigners and they shall scatter her and empty her land, for they were against her all around on the day of evil.
To wherever I say, the archer shall bend his bow, and he shall not be healed with his coat of mail, and have no pity on her youths, destroy all her host.
And they shall fall slain in the land of the Kasdim, and those thrust through in her streets.
For Yisroel is not widowed, neither is Yehudah widowed from his Elokim, Havayah of Hosts, for their land is full of guilt, from the Holy One of Yisroel.
Flee from within Bavel and each one save his life, be not cut off in her iniquity; for it is the time of Havayah's vengeance; He is paying her a recompense.
Bavel is a golden cup in Havayah's hand, it intoxicates all the earth; nations have drunk of her wine, therefore, nations are mad.
Suddenly, Bavel has fallen and has been broken; wail over her, take balm for her pain, perhaps she may be healed.
"We treated Bavel, but she was not cured. Leave her and let us go each one to his own land, for her judgment has touched the sky and has been raised to the heavens."
"The Havayah has brought out our merits; come and let us tell in Tziyon the deed of Havayah our Elokim."
Polish the arrows, fill the quivers; Havayah has aroused the desire of the kings of Madai, for His aim is to destroy her, for Havayah's vengeance is the vegeance of His Temple.
On the walls of Bavel raise a standard, strengthen the watch, station sentries, prepare the ambushes, for Havayah both planned and did what He had spoken concerning the inhabitants of Bavel.
You, who dwell by many waters, abundant in treasures, your end has come, the measure of your violence.
The Havayah of Hosts has sworn by Himself; I have indeed filled you with men as with locusts, and they shall raise a battle-cry against you.
He Who has made the earth with His strength, He prepared the world by His wisdom, and with His understanding He stretched out the heavens.
At the sound of His giving a multitude of waters in the heaven, He brought up clouds from the end of the earth, He made lightning for the rain, and He took wind out of His treasuries.
Every man is brutish without knowledge; every smith is put to shame by his graven image, for his molten images are false, without spirit in them.
They are vanity, a work of delusion; at the time of their visitation, they shall perish.
Not like these is Yackov's portion, for He is the One Who formed everything, and the tribe of His inheritance; Havayah of Hosts is His name.
You are for Me a shatterer, yea weapons of war, and with you I would shatter nations, and with you I would destroy kingdoms.
And with you I would shatter a horse and his rider, and with you I would shatter a chariot and its rider.
And with you I would shatter man and woman, and with you I would shatter elder and youth, and with you I would shatter young man and virgin.
And with you I would shatter a shepherd and his flock, and with you I would shatter a farmer and his team, and with you I would shatter governors and officers.
And I will recompense Bavel and all the inhabitants of the land of the Kasdim for all their evil that they committed in Tziyon before your eyes, Havayah says.
Behold I am against you, O destroying mountain, Havayah says, who destroys all the earth, and I will stretch out My hand upon you and roll you down from the rocks and make you a burnt mountain.
And they shall take from you neither a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations, for you shall be desolate forever, Havayah says.

Raise up a standard in the land, sound a shofar among the nations, prepare nations against her, gather against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz; appoint over her a marshal, bring up horses like bristling locusts.
Prepare nations against her, the kings of Madai, her governors, and all her officers, and all the land of his rule.
And the earth quaked and was in pain for the plans of Havayah rose upon Bavel to make the land of Bavel desolate without an inhabitant.
The mighty men of Bavel ceased to wage war, they dwelt in the fortresses, their might has failed, they have become like women; her dwellings were ignited, her bars broken.
One courier runs to meet another courier, and one herald to meet another herald, to tell the king of Bavel that his city has been taken from the end,
and the fords have been seized, and the reeds have been burnt with fire, and the warriors have been frightened.
For so Havayah of Hosts said, the Elokim of Yisroel; The daughter of Bavel is like a granary at the time it is threshed. A little more time and the time of harvest shall come to her.

Nevuchadretzar the king of Bavel, has devoured me, he has crushed me; yea he has placed me as an empty vessel; he has swallowed me like a sea monster, he has filled his belly with my delicacies; he has rinsed me out.
"May the plundering done me and my food be upon Bavel!" says the dweller of Tziyon, "and my blood upon the dwellers of the land of the Kasdim!" says Yerushalayim.
Therefore, so Havayah said: Behold I plead your cause, and I avenge your vengeance, and I will dry up her sea and dry up her fountain.
And Bavel shall become heaps, a den of jackals, a desolation and a hissing without an inhabitant.
Together they roar like young lions, they growl like lion cubs.
In their heat I will place their wine feasts, and I will make them drunk in order that they become joyful, and sleep a perpetual sleep and not awaken, Havayah says.
I will lower them like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with he-goats.
How was Sheishach taken and the praise of all the earth seized? How did Bavel become an astonishment among the nations?
The sea has ascended upon Bavel; with the multitude of its waves it has been covered.
Her cities became desolate, a dry land and a desert, a land where no man dwells, neither does any man pass through them.
And I will visit retribution on Bel in Bavel, and I will take what he has swallowed out of his mouth, and nations shall no longer stream to him: even the wall of Bavel has fallen.
Go out of its midst, My people, and each one save his life, from the burning wrath of Havayah.

And lest your heart be faint and you fear because of the rumor that is heard in the land, for a rumor shall come one year, and after it in a year a rumor, and violence in the land, and one ruler upon another ruler.
Therefore, behold days are coming, and I will visit retribution on the graven images of Bavel, and all her land shall be shamed, and all her slain shall fall in her midst.
And heaven and earth and all that is in them shall sing for joy, for spoilers shall come upon her from the north, Havayah says.
As Bavel caused the slain of Yisroel to fall, so in Bavel shall fall the slain of all the land.
Fugitives from the sword, go, do not stand still! Remember Havayah from the distant past, and let Yerushalayim enter your mind.
"We are ashamed for we have heard reproach, embarrassment has covered our faces, for strangers have come upon the sanctuaries of the house of Havayah."
Therefore, behold days are coming, Havayah says, and I will visit retribution upon her graven images and throughout her land the mortally wounded shall groan.
Should Bavel ascend to heaven and should she fortify the height of her strength, from Me shall spoilers come upon her, Havayah says.
Hark! A cry from Bavel, and great destruction from the land of the Kasdim.
For Havayah is spoiling Bavel and He has put an end to her great din, and their waves roared like many waters, the stirring of their voice was uttered.
For a spoiler has come upon her, yea upon Bavel, and her mighty men have been seized, their bows have been broken, for Havayah is a Elokim of recompenses, He shall surely requite.
And I will make drunk her princes and her wise men, her governors and her mighty men, and they shall sleep a perpetual sleep and not awaken, says the King, Havayah of Hosts is His Name.

So Havayah of Hosts said: The broad walls of Bavel shall be overthrown and her lofty gates shall be burnt with fire, and peoples shall labor for much futility, and kingdoms in much fire, and they shall be weary.

The word that Yirmiyahu the prophet commanded Serayah the son of Neiriyah the son of Machseiyah, when he went with Tzidkiyahu the king of Yehudah to Bavel in the fourth year of his reign, and Serayah was the prince of tribute.
And Yirmiyahu wrote all the evil that would befall Bavel in one scroll, all these words that are written concerning Bavel.
And Yirmiyahu said to Serayah, "When you come to Bavel, you shall see and read all these words.
And you shall say, 'O Havayah, You have spoken concerning this place to cut it off, that it have no inhabitant, either man or beast, but it shall be forever desolate.'
And it shall come to pass that when you finish reading this scroll, you shall tie a stone to it and cast it into the Peras.
And you shall say, 'So shall Bavel sink and not rise, because of the evil that I bring upon her, and they shall weary." Until here are the words of Yirmiyahu.
Tzidkiyahu was twenty — one years old when he became king, and his mother's name was Chamutal the daughter of Yirmiyahu from Libnah.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of Havayah, like all that Yehoyakim had done.
Because the wrath of Havayah was against Yerushalayim and against Yehudah until He cast them away from before His presence, Tzidkiyahu rebelled against the king of Bavel.

And it was in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, that Nevuchadretzar the king of Bavel came, he and his entire army, against Yerushalayim and encamped against it, and they built works of siege around it.
And the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Tzidkiyahu.
In the fourth month, on the ninth of the month, the famine became severe in the city, and the people of the land had no food.

The city was broken into, and all the men of war fled and emerged from the city at night by way of the gate between the two walls that was near the king's garden, and the Kasdim were surrounding the city, and they went by way of the Aravah.
And the army of the Kasdim pursued the king, and they overtook Tzidkiyahu on the plains of Yericho, and all his army had scattered and deserted him.
And they seized the king and brought him up to the king of Bavel, to Rivlah in the land of Chamas, and called him to account.
And the king of Bavel slaughtered Tzidkiyahu's sons before his eyes, and also, all the princes of Yehudah he slaughtered in Rivlah.
And he blinded Tzidkiyahu's eyes, and he bound him with copper chains and brought him to the king of Bavel, to Bavel, and he placed him in the prison until the day of his death.

And in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month that was the nineteenth year of King Nevuchadretzar the king of Bavel — Nevuzaradan the chief executioner, came and stood before the king of Bavel in Yerushalayim.
And he burnt the house of Havayah and the king's palace, and all the houses of Yerushalayim and all the houses of the dignitaries he burnt with fire.
The entire army of the Kasdim that was with the chief executioner demolished all the walls of Yerushalayim around.

And Nevuzaradan the chief executioner exiled some of the poorest of the people and the remnant of the people who remained in the city, and the defectors who defected to the king of Bavel, and the rest of the populace.
Now the chief executioner left over some of the poorest of the land as vine-dressers and farmers.
And the Kasdim broke the copper pillars that were in the house of Havayah and the bases and the copper sea that was in the house of Havayah, and they carried off all their copper to Bavel.
And they took the pots and the shovels and the musical instruments and the basins and the spoons and all the copper vessels with which they served.
And the chief executioner took the pitchers, the censers, the basins, the pots, the candelabra, the spoons, and the frames both of gold and of silver.
The two pillars, the one sea, and the cattle that were beside the bases that Shlomo had made for the house of Havayah; there was no weight for the copper of all these vessels.
And the pillars — the height of one pillar was eighteen cubits and a thread of twelve cubits would encircle it, and its thickness was four fingers, hollow.

And there was a capital of copper upon it, and the height of the one capital was five cubits, and a net, and pomegranates on the capital around, all was copper. And such did the second pillar have, and pomegranates.
And the pomegranates were ninety-six to the outside; all the pomegranates were one hundred on the net all around.
And the chief executioner took Serayah the head priest and Tzefanyah the priest of second rank, and the three keepers of the utensils.

And from the city he took one eunuch who was appointed over the men of war, and seven men of those who saw the king's face, who were found in the city, and the scribe of the general of the army, who would muster out the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the midst of the city.
And Nevuzaradan the chief executioner took them and brought them to the king of Bavel, to Rivlah.
And the king of Bavel struck them down and killed them in Rivlah in the land of Chamas, and Yehudah went into exile off its land.
This is the people whom Nevuchadretzar exiled in the seventh year: Yehudim three thousand and twenty-three.
In the eighteenth year of Nevuchadretzar, he exiled from Yerushalayim eight hundred and thirty — two people.
In the twenty — third year of Nevuchadretzar, Nevuzaradan the chief executioner exiled of the Yehudim seven hundred and forty-five souls, all the souls totaled four thousand and six hundred.

And it was in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Yehoyachin king of Yehudah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, that Evil-Merodach, king of Bavel, in the year of his coronation, lifted up the head of Yehoyachin, king of Yehudah and released him from prison.
And he spoke with him kindly and placed his throne above the throne of the kings who were with him in Bavel.
And he changed his prison garb, and he ate meals before him regularly all the days of his life.
And his meals, regular meals were given him from the king of Bavel, each day's need in its day, all the days of his life.
